अथातो
अथातो वातव्याधिनिदानं
अथातो वातव्याधिनिदानं व्याख्यास्यामः
यथोवाच
यथोवाच भगवान्
यथोवाच भगवान् धन्वन्तरिः

1. अथ — अव्ययम् — मङ्गलादौ (now) [R1]
2. अतः — अव्ययम् — हेतौ (therefore) [R1]
3. वातव्याधिनिदानम् — सुबन्तः — नपुंसकलिङ्गम् द्वितीया एकवचनम् [R1]
4. व्याख्यास्यामः — तिङन्तः — लृट्, उत्तमपुरुषः, बहुवचनम् [R1]
5. यथा — अव्ययम् — प्रकारे (as) [R1]
6. उवाच — तिङन्तः — लिट्, प्रथमपुरुषः, एकवचनम् [R1]
7. भगवान् — सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् प्रथमा एकवचनम् [R1]
8. धन्वन्तरिः — सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् प्रथमा एकवचनम् [R1]
भगवान् धन्वन्तरिः यथा उवाच, अथ अतः वातव्याधिनिदानं व्याख्यास्यामः।

भगवान् = the Lord, revered | धन्वन्तरिः = Dhanvantari | यथा = as | उवाच = spoke | अथ = now | अतः = therefore | वातव्याधिनिदानम् = the diagnosis of the diseases caused by Vata | व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall explain |

Sentence meaning: As the revered Lord Dhanvantari spoke, now therefore we shall explain the diagnosis of the diseases caused by Vata.

At the very outset of the निदानस्थान (Diagnosis Section) of the सुश्रुतसंहिता, the author announces the commencement of the chapter dedicated to वातव्याधि (diseases caused by aggravated Vata) [R1]. By attributing the teachings directly to भगवान् धन्वन्तरि, the text establishes the absolute authority, authenticity, and divine transmission of the medical knowledge that follows [R1]. This introductory utterance sets the formal scope of the chapter, fulfilling the traditional academic and spiritual requirement of stating the subject matter before its detailed exposition.

पद: अथ
Synonyms: अनन्तरम्, मङ्गले, आरम्भे
Grammar: अव्ययम् — मङ्गलादौ (now) [R1]
धातु: इण् (गतौ) | धात्वर्थ: going / beginning
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Marks the auspicious beginning of the treatise following the introductory homage. [R1]

पद: अतः
Synonyms: अस्मात्, हेतौ
Grammar: अव्ययम् — हेतौ (therefore) [R1]
धातु: इण् (गतौ) | धात्वर्थ: going / causation
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Establishes the causal connection with the preceding context of approaching the teacher. [R1]

पद: वातव्याधिनिदानम्
Synonyms: वातजन्यरोगाणां कारणं, वातविकारपरीक्षा
Grammar: सुबन्तः — नपुंसकलिङ्गम् द्वितीया एकवचनम् [R1]
समासविग्रह: वातानां व्याधयः वातव्याधयः (षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः); वातव्याधीनां निदानम् वातव्याधिनिदानम् (षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः)
धातु: वा (गतौ गन्धने च), व्याधू (कम्पनविवर्तनयोः), नि + दा (अवखण्डने) | धात्वर्थ: moving, agitating, determining the root cause
उपसर्ग: नि
Contribution: Directly specifies the clinical focus of the text on the origin and manifestation of Vata disorders. [R1]

पद: व्याख्यास्यामः
Synonyms: प्रतिपादयिष्यामः, कथयिष्यामः
Grammar: तिङन्तः — लृट्, उत्तमपुरुषः, बहुवचनम् [R1]
धातु: ख्या (प्रकथने) | धात्वर्थ: to speak publicly or explain
उपसर्ग: वि + आङ् — वि denotes distribution/detail, आङ् denotes completeness (comprehensive exposition)
Contribution: The plural verb indicates the authoritative collective teaching of the tradition through the preceptor and disciple. [R1]

पद: यथा
Synonyms: येन प्रकारेण, येन विधिना
Grammar: अव्ययम् — प्रकारे (as) [R1]
धातु: हा (त्यागे) | धात्वर्थ: leaving / manner
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Subordinates the upcoming clause to the foundational teaching received from the divine source. [R1]

पद: उवाच
Synonyms: कथयामास, प्राह
Grammar: तिङन्तः — लिट्, प्रथमपुरुषः, एकवचनम् [R1]
धातु: वच् (परिभाषे) | धात्वर्थ: to speak or declare
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Validates the statements as direct historical and medical revelation uttered by the primary authority. [R1]

पद: भगवान्
Synonyms: ऐश्वर्यवान्, पूज्यः, ईश्वरः
Grammar: सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् प्रथमा एकवचनम् [R1]
समासविग्रह: भगः (ऐश्वर्यं धर्मो यशः श्रीश्च ज्ञानवैराग्ययोश्च यत्) अस्यास्तीति भगवान् (मत्वर्थीयप्रत्ययः)
धातु: भज् (सेवायाम्) | धात्वर्थ: to possess supreme qualities/glory
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Attributes divine majesty and omniscience to the speaker, reinforcing the absolute reliability of Ayurveda. [R1]

पद: धन्वन्तरिः
Synonyms: सुदासः, काशिराजः, अमृतोद्भवः
Grammar: सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् प्रथमा एकवचनम् [R1]
धातु: धन् (गतौ), तॄ (प्लवनतरणयोः) | धात्वर्थ: moving swiftly, helping across (samsara/disease)
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Identifies the historical and divine incarnate source of surgery and medicine who bestows healing. [R1]

By initiating the Nidana Sthana with the explicit mention of Vata vyadhi, the Acharya subtly indicates that among all pathological factors, Vata possesses the most erratic and primary capacity for initiating complex systemic disorders [R1]. The choice of the plural verb व्याख्यास्यामः combined with the direct attribution to भगवान् धन्वन्तरि establishes a clinical methodology where empirical observation merges seamlessly with divine tradition to decode elusive neural and locomotor pathologies [R1]. Furthermore, placing this text at the very forefront of the diagnostic section underscores that mastering the erratic nature of Vata is the absolute prerequisite for clinical competence in managing chronic diseases [R1].

1st पाद- दोषधात्वग्निसमतां
2nd पाद- सम्प्राप्तिं विषयेषु च
3rd पाद- क्रियाणामानुलोम्यं च
4th पाद- करोत्यकुपितोऽनिलः
पाठान्तरम्: इन्द्रियार्थोपसम्प्राप्तिं | दोषधात्वग्न्यवैकृतम् | क्रियाणामानुलोम्यं च | कुर्याद्वायुरदूषितः

1. दोषधात्वग्निसमताम् — सुबन्तः — स्त्रीलिङ्गम् द्वितीया एकवचनम्
2. सम्प्राप्तिम् — सुबन्तः — स्त्रीलिङ्गम् द्वितीया एकवचनम्
3. विषयेषु — सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् सप्तमी बहुवचनम्
4. च — अव्ययम् — समुच्चयद्योतकम् (and)
5. क्रियाणाम् — सुबन्तः — स्त्रीलिङ्गम् षष्ठी बहुवचनम्
6. आनुलोम्यम् — सुबन्तः — नपुंसकलिङ्गम् द्वितीया एकवचनम्
7. च — अव्ययम् — समुच्चयद्योतकम् (and)
8. करोति — तिङन्तः — लट्, प्रथमपुरुषः, एकवचनम् (परस्मैपदी)
9. अकुपितः — सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् प्रथमा एकवचनम्
10. अनिलः — सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् प्रथमा एकवचनम्
अकुपितः अनिलः दोषधात्वग्निसमतां विषयेषु सम्प्राप्तिं च क्रियाणाम् आनुलोम्यं च करोति [R1]

अकुपितः = not provoked / tranquil | अनिलः = Vata / wind | दोषधात्वग्निसमताम् = the state of equilibrium of doshas, dhatus, and agnis | विषयेषु = in sensory objects | सम्प्राप्तिम् = proper attainment / perception | च = and | क्रियाणाम् = of bodily functions / actions | आनुलोम्यम् = regularity / proper direction | च = and | करोति = performs / does [R1]

When not provoked, Vata performs the equilibrium of doshas, dhatus, and agnis, the proper perception of sensory objects, and the regularity of bodily functions [R1].

In the Nidana Sthana of the सुश्रुतसंहिता, while describing the normal physiological actions of movement within the body, the author explains the state of ānila when it remains unprovoked [R1]. When अनिल is अकुपित, it sustains the equilibrium of दोष, धातु, and अग्नि, ensures the proper perception of objects by the senses, and maintains the normal downward and orderly direction of all bodily functions [R1]. Thus, the author intends to highlight that a tranquil and unvitiated वायु is the fundamental basis for maintaining health and physiological harmony [R1].

पद: दोषधात्वग्निसमताम्
Synonyms: दोषधातूनाम् अग्नेश्च समता, साम्यम्
Grammar: स्त्रीलिङ्गम्, द्वितीया एकवचनम् (कर्मणि द्वितीया); समासः: दोषाश्च धातवश्च अग्नयश्च = दोषधात्वग्नयः (इतरेतरद्वन्द्वः), तेषां समता = दोषधात्वग्निसमता (षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः)
धातु: सम् (उपसर्गपूर्विका इण् गतौ वा, अथवा सम-धातुः) | धात्वर्थः: to be even, balanced
उपसर्ग: समू (सम्यक्)
Contribution: The compound form emphasizes the simultaneous and harmonious equilibrium of the three core physiological pillars (dosha, dhatu, agni) maintained by normal Vata.

पद: सम्प्राप्तिम्
Synonyms: प्राप्तिः, अनुभवः, सम्यक् प्राप्तिः
Grammar: स्त्रीलिङ्गम्, द्वितीया एकवचनम्
धातु: आप् (व्याप्तौ) | धात्वर्थः: to reach, attain, obtain
उपसर्ग: सम् (सम्यक्)
Contribution: The prefix 'सम्' highlights complete, accurate, and unhindered sensory perception, indicating clarity of mind and senses when Vata is calm.

पद: विषयेषु
Synonyms: शब्दादिषु, इन्द्रियार्थेषु
Grammar: पुंलिङ्गम्, सप्तमी बहुवचनम्
धातु: विष् (व्याप्तौ) | धात्वर्थः: to occupy, pervade, objects of senses
उपसर्ग: निर् (वि + इष् वा - conventional noun form)
Contribution: Locative plural specifies the external sensory domains (sound, touch, form, taste, smell) where Vata ensures proper cognitive contact.

पद: च
Synonyms: तथा, अपि
Grammar: अव्ययम् (समुच्चयद्योतकम्)
धातु: no root (अव्यय) | धात्वर्थः: conjunction
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Connects multiple physiological outcomes produced by Vata, ensuring structural balance alongside sensory and functional order.

पद: क्रियाणाम्
Synonyms: कर्माणाम्, चेष्टानाम्
Grammar: स्त्रीलिङ्गम्, षष्ठी बहुवचनम् (from क्रिया)
धातु: कृ (करणे) | धात्वर्थः: to do, make, act
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Genitive plural governs all bodily movements and organic functions regulated under Vata's jurisdiction.

पद: आनुलोम्यम्
Synonyms: प्रकृतानुसरणं, अनुलौकिकता, सद्वृत्तिः
Grammar: नपुंसकलिङ्गम्, द्वितीया एकवचनम् (तद्धित्तान्तः / भावनाम)
धातु: अनु + लम् (गतौ) | धात्वर्थः: moving along the natural path or direction
उपसर्ग: अनु
Contribution: Signifies the smooth, downward, and orderly flow of bodily functions without obstruction or reversal (such as udavarta).

पद: च
Synonyms: तथा, अपि
Grammar: अव्ययम् (समुच्चयद्योतकम्)
धातु: no root (अव्यय) | धात्वर्थः: conjunction
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Links functional regularity seamlessly with the earlier mentioned equilibrium and sensory perception.

पद: करोति
Synonyms: सम्पादयति, विरचयति
Grammar: लट् (वर्तमानकालः), प्रथमपुरुषः, एकवचनम्, परस्मैपदम्
धातु: कृ (ञिञ् करणे) | धात्वर्थः: to perform, execute, bring about
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: The active verb highlights Vata as the dynamic engine and active agent responsible for all physiological maintenance in the body.

पद: अकुपितः
Synonyms: प्रकुपितभिन्नः, प्रश्रितः, अनुपहतः, अदूषितः
Grammar: पुंलिङ्गम्, प्रथमा एकवचनम् (कर्मधारय / बहुव्रीहिः - नञ्समासः)
धातु: कुप् (क्रोधे सञ्जातकोपे च) | धात्वर्थः: to be agitated, provoked
उपसर्ग: नञ् (अ) negation
Contribution: The negative prefix specifies that health and homeostasis are the results of Vata remaining undisturbed and in its natural, non-aggravated state.

पद: अनिलः
Synonyms: वायुः, मारुतः, समीरणः
Grammar: पुंलिङ्गम्, प्रथमा एकवचनम्
धातु: अन् (प्राणने) | धात्वर्थः: to breathe, move, blow
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Names the specific biological force (Vata) whose inherent dynamic motion maintains life when uncorrupted.

By highlighting that an unprovoked Vata maintains 'आनुलोम्यम्' (smooth downward flow), the Acharya implicitly establishes that all disease pathology essentially begins with 'प्रतिलोमगति' (reversal of normal movement), such as in Udavarta. Furthermore, pairing 'दोषधात्वग्निसमताम्' with 'विषयेषु सम्प्राप्तिम्' reveals the profound Ayurvedic principle that both somatic homeostasis and cognitive-sensory clarity are entirely dependent upon the uninterrupted, tranquil dynamics of Vayu.

1st पाद- यथाऽग्निः पञ्चधा भिन्नो
2nd पाद- नामस्थानक्रियामयैः
3rd पाद- भिन्नोऽनिलस्तस्था ह्येको
4th पाद- नामस्थानक्रियामयैः

1. यथा — अव्ययम् — उपमायां (just as)
2. अग्निः — सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् प्रथमा एकवचनम्
3. पञ्चधा — अव्ययम् — प्रकारे (in five ways)
4. भिन्नः — सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् प्रथमा एकवचनम् (क्तान्तम्)
5. नामस्थानक्रियामयैः — सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् तृतीया बहुवचनम्
6. भिन्नः — सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् प्रथमा एकवचनम् (क्तान्तम्)
7. अनिलः — सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् प्रथमा एकवचनम्
8. तथा — अव्ययम् — प्रकारे (thus, similarly)
9. हि — अव्ययम् — अवधारणेलङ्कारे (indeed)
10. एकः — सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् प्रथमा एकवचनम्
11. नामस्थानक्रियामयैः — सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् तृतीया बहुवचनम्
यथा अग्निः नामस्थानक्रियामयैः पञ्चधा भिन्नः, तथा हि एकः अनिलः नामस्थानक्रियामयैः भिन्नः।

यथा = just as | अग्निः = fire | नामस्थानक्रियामयैः = by names, sites, and functions | पञ्चधा = in five ways | भिन्नः = divided | तथा = thus | हि = indeed | एकः = single | अनिलः = wind (Vata) | नामस्थानक्रियामयैः = by names, sites, and functions | भिन्नः = divided | 

Just as fire, though single, is divided in five ways by names, sites, and functions, thus indeed a single wind (Vata) is divided by names, sites, and functions.

In this verse from the निदानस्थान of the सुश्रुतसंहिता, the Acharya explains the fundamental nature of वातः by drawing an analogy with अग्निः [R1]. Just as fire, although fundamentally one, is diversified into five distinct forms based on its names, anatomical sites, and specific functions, the single wind (वातः) is similarly divided into five types [R1]. This establishes that while वातः is a unified entity circulating in the body, it operates in five specialized categories—such as प्राणः, उदानः, समानः, व्यानः, and अपानः—to sustain living beings [R1, R3].

पद: यथा
Synonyms: येन प्रकारेण, सदृशम्
Grammar: अव्ययम् (उपमाद्यर्थे)
धातु: न/अ | धात्वर्थ: अव्यय
उपसर्ग: न
Contribution: Establishes a direct simile between the behavior of fire and Vata [R1].

पद: अग्निः
Synonyms: वह्निः, पावकः, ज्वलनः
Grammar: सुबन्तः, पुंलिङ्गम्, प्रथमा, एकवचनम्
धातु: अग् | धात्वर्थ: गतौ, दीप्तौ च
उपसर्ग: न
Contribution: Serves as the primary standard of comparison, illustrating how a single entity manifests in five forms [R1].

पद: पञ्चधा
Synonyms: पञ्चप्रकारैः, पञ्चशः
Grammar: अव्ययम् (प्रकारे तद्धितप्रत्ययान्तः)
धातु: पञ्चन् | धात्वर्थ: संख्या
उपसर्ग: न
Contribution: Quantifies the division precisely into five modalities of Vata and fire [R1].

पद: भिन्नः
Synonyms: विदीर्णः, पृथक्कृतः, विविधः
Grammar: सुबन्तः, पुंलिङ्गम्, प्रथमा, एकवचनम् (क्तान्तम्)
धातु: भिद् | धात्वर्थ: विदारणे
उपसर्ग: न
Contribution: Indicates that the division is functional and positional, not an absolute fragmentation of the single essence [R1].

पद: नामस्थानक्रियामयैः
Synonyms: नामभिः स्थानैः क्रियाभिश्च मयैः (युक्तैः)

पद: एकः

Grammar: सुबन्तः, पुंलिङ्गम्, प्रथमा, एकवचनम्
धातु: इक् | धात्वर्थ: गतौ
उपसर्ग: न
Contribution: Emphasizes the fundamental unity of Vata despite its diverse anatomical and functional manifestations [R1].

By choosing अग्निः as the standard of comparison, the आचार्य hints that just as fire's division into forms like पचन (pachana) does not destroy its singular elemental essence, वायुः remains inherently unified despite its fivefold operational division [R1]. The repetition of नामस्थानक्रियामयैः underscores that a clinician must evaluate disease not merely through generalized systemic symptoms, but by precisely localizing the disturbance to the specific anatomical site and functional modality of the afflicted subtype [R1, R3]. Furthermore, by establishing वायुः as a single entity that only appears fragmented due to its diverse loci and actions, the आचार्य implies that vitiation in one sub-type can dynamically cascade across others due to their shared underlying continuum [R1, R6].

स्थानस्थाः = staying in their respective places | पञ्च = five | मारुताः = winds | प्राणोदानौ = Prana and Udana | समानः = Samana | व्यानः = Vyana | अपानः = Apana | च = and | शरीरिणम् = the embodied one / living being | यापयन्ति = maintain / cause to live [R1]

The five winds, staying in their respective places—Prana, Udana, Samana, Vyana, and Apana—maintain the embodied one [R1].

In the context of the classification of वायु in the सुश्रुतसंहिता निदानस्थान, the author explains that while the single vital wind operates in five different ways like fire, its five specific forms—प्राण, उदान, समान, व्यान, and अपान—staying in their respective locations, sustain and maintain the embodied living being [R1]. Thus, the normal physiological existence of an individual fundamentally depends on the coordinated, site-specific functioning of these five marutas [R1].

The employment of the term 'स्थानस्थाः' coupled with 'एव' underscores a critical physiological precondition: the maintenance of the embodied state depends strictly upon each sub-dosha remaining anchored within its dedicated anatomical seat. The Acharya deliberately uses the causative verb 'यापयन्ति' rather than a simple active form, implying that life is not merely an inherent spark, but an actively sustained, continuous process driven by the dynamic equilibrium of these pneumatic forces. Furthermore, the systematic grouping through successive conjunctions ('च') reveals a holistic view of the body, where the failure of even a single localized wind threatens the operational integrity of the entire living organism.

यः = which [R1] | वायुः = wind / vayu [R1] | वक्त्रसञ्चारी = moving in the mouth [R1] | सः = that [R1] | प्राणः = named Prana [R1] | नाम = by name [R1] | देहधृक् = sustainer of the body [R1] | सः = that [R1] | अन्नम् = food [R1] | अन्तः = inside [R1] | प्रवेशयति = causes to enter [R1] | प्राणान् = lives / life-breaths [R1] | च = and [R1] | अपि = also [R1] | अवलम्बते = supports [R1]

Which wind moving in the mouth, that is named Prana and is the sustainer of the body; that causes food to enter inside and also supports the life-breaths.

In the context of the fivefold classification of vayu that sustains the living body within the Nidana Sthana of the Sushruta Samhita, this verse defines the specific function of प्राणवायु [R1, R5]. The author explains that the vayu moving in the mouth is known as प्राण, which acts as the sustainer of the body [R1]. Its primary physiological actions are to facilitate the entry of food inward and to support the vital life-breaths [R1].

By designating the breath moving in the mouth as देहधृक्, the आचार्य hints that structural integrity of the physical form relies fundamentally on the continuous intake occurring at the upper portal of the body [R1]. The choice of the root धृञ् combined with the plural use of प्राणान् reveals that the localized oral current is not merely an isolated pneumatic draft, but the primary anchor upon which all other systemic vital faculties depend for their ongoing existence [R1]. Furthermore, by coupling the mechanical act of forcing food inward (अन्नं प्रवेशयति) with the metaphysical support of life-breaths (प्राणांश्चाप्यवलम्बते), the author subtly establishes a direct physiological continuum between external nutritional intake and internal vitality [R1].

Which best among winds, Udana by name, indeed goes upwards, that vitiated one mostly produces diseases such as hiccup and dyspnoea.

In this verse from the निदानस्थान of सुश्रुतसंहिता, आचार्य सुश्रुत explains the normal and pathological functions of the उदान वायु within the context of vata bheda in रोगनिश्चय. When the best among winds, known as उदान, moves in its natural upward direction, it performs its normal physiological functions in the upper body [R1]. However, when this उदान वायु becomes vitiated or provoked, it predominantly gives rise to specific upper-body disorders such as हिक्का (hiccup) and श्वास (dyspnoea) [R1]. Thus, the author highlights how the vitiation of upward-moving wind acts as the primary causative factor for these affliction types in the upper regions [R1].

By designating this specific breath as पवनोत्तम, the आचार्य implies that while all bodily winds are essential, the upward-moving vital force holds a pre-eminent position in governing the upper anatomical gateways and governing higher physiological faculties. The strategic use of the term प्रायशः underscores a deterministic vulnerability: whenever this specific upward current becomes deranged, it unfailingly targets the respiratory pathways, making conditions like hiccup and dyspnoea the most predictable and primary clinical manifestations of its vitiation. Furthermore, by linking its inherent upward trajectory directly to the genesis of diseases restricted to the upper body, the text hints that the anatomical seat of the pathology is a direct extension of the vector of its movement.

Grammar: अव्ययम् — तसिलादिप्रत्ययान्तम् (विशेष शब्दात् तस् प्रत्ययः बाहुल्ये/विशेषे) [R1]
धातु: विश् (प्रवेशने) | धात्वर्थ: to enter, to distinguish, to specialize [R1]
उपसर्ग: वि (distinctly) [R1]
Contribution: Highlights that while general effects exist, the upper-clavicular diseases are a preeminent and characteristic hallmark of udana vayu vitiation [R1].

The आचार्य intentionally connects the higher intellectual and artistic faculties like speech and song with the region above the collarbone, indicating that *Udana Vata* is the primary driving force behind all expression originating from the throat and head [R1]. By utilizing the double prefix in *अभिप्रवर्तते*, the text suggests that when this vital air is balanced, it forcefully propels upward energy to manifest clear communication, whereas its vitiation directly targets this very same pathway to afflict the upper body with specialized disorders [R1]. Thus, the verse subtly reveals that the physiological seat of human art and communication is simultaneously the most vulnerable locus for *Udana*-derived pathologies [R1].

सः = he (the samana vayu) [R1] | आमपक्वाशयचरः = moving in the stomach and intestines [R1] | वह्निसङ्गतः = united with the digestive fire [R1] | समानः = Samana vayu [R1] | अन्नम् = food [R1] | पचति = digests [R1] | तत्जान् = born from that (food) [R1] | च = and [R1] | विशेषान् = specific elements or essences [R1] | विविनक्ति = separates [R1] | हि = indeed [R1]

सः आमपक्वाशयचरः वह्निसङ्गतः समानः अन्नं पचति, तत्जान् च विशेषान् विविनक्ति हि [R1].

In this verse from the *Nidana Sthana* of the *Sushruta Samhita*, the author explains the specific physiological function of समानवायु within the context of the types and locations of *Vata* [R1]. Moving between the *Amapakvashaya* (stomach and intestines) and in close association with the *Agni* (digestive fire), *Samana Vayu* digests the consumed food and effectively separates its essential nutrients from the waste products [R1]. Thus, it plays a vital role in proper digestion and metabolism before any pathological disturbances are detailed in the subsequent verses [R1].

By placing *समानः* between *आमपक्वाशयचरः* and *वह्निंसङ्गतः*, the आचार्य hints that *Vata* does not merely fan the digestive fire from a distance, but physically bridges the upper and lower receptacles of digestion to contain the heat right where transformation is required [R1]. The choice of the root *विच्* through *विविनक्ति* reveals a selective intelligence inherent in *Samana*, implying that it acts as a discriminating gatekeeper that actively sorts the refined essence from the dregs rather than just passively allowing a chemical breakdown [R1]. Furthermore, the emphatic particle *हि* signals an absolute physiological rule that without this specific convergence of *Vata* and *Agni* in the central axis, neither cellular nourishment nor proper excretion can ever be initiated [R1].

कृत्स्नदेहचरः रससंवहनोद्यतः व्यानः गुल्माग्निसादातीसारप्रभृतीन् गदान् कुरुते।

कृत्स्नदेहचरः = moving in the entire body [R1] | रससंवहनोद्यतः = engaged in the circulation of rasa (nutrient fluid) [R1] | व्यानः = the vyana vayu [R1] | गुल्माग्निसादातीसारप्रभृतीन् = such as gulma, agnisada (diminution of digestive fire), atisara (diarrhea), and others [R1] | गदान् = diseases [R1] | कुरुते = creates / causes [R1]

Moving in the entire body and engaged in the circulation of rasa, the vyana vayu creates diseases such as gulma, agnisada, and atisara.

In the context of describing the specific locations and pathological manifestations of the sub-doshas of vata within the Nidana Sthana of the सुश्रुतसंहिता, this verse explains the morbid consequences of a vitiated व्यान वायु [R1]. Normally engaged in circulating रस through the entire body, when provoked, this vata gives rise to systemic and local disorders such as गुल्म, अग्निसाद्, and अतिसार [R1]. Thus, the author highlights how the impairment of व्यान's circulatory function directly disrupts bodily stability and precipitates various gastrointestinal and systemic pathologies [R1].

By designating व्यान as 'कृत्स्नदेहचरः' and 'रससंवहनोद्यतः', आचार्य सुश्रुत subtly hints that any obstruction in the pervasive circulation of रस directly compromises the agni located at the roots of nutrition, thereby explaining why a circulatory defect paradoxically manifests as gastrointestinal disorders like गुल्म and अतिसार [R1]. The choice of the word 'उद्यतः' implies an inherent, ceaseless physiological striving that, when thwarted by vitiation, rebounds systemically across the entire physical frame [R1].

In this context of describing the locations and functions of the five types of Vata within the Nidana Sthana, the author explains the specific physiological and pathological roles of व्यान [R1]. Normally, व्यान regulates circulation, facilitates movements in five ways, and causes the discharge of sweat and blood throughout the body [R1]. However, when it becomes aggravated (क्रुद्ध), it generally produces various diseases that spread across the entire body [R1].

पक्वाधानालयः = having the large intestine (pakvashaya) as its abode [R1] | अपानः = Apana Vayu [R1] | समीरणः = the moving wind / Vayu [R1] | काले = at the proper time [R1] | शकृन्मूत्रम् = faeces and urine [R1] | शुक्रगर्भार्तवानि = semen, foetus, and menstrual blood [R1] | च = and [R1] | अधः = downwards [R1] | अपि = also [R1] | च = and [R1] | कर्षति = draws / moves [R1]
Sentence meaning: The Apana Vayu, whose abode is the large intestine, at the proper time draws downwards faeces, urine, semen, foetus, and menstrual blood.

Within the context of the *वातव्याधिनिदान* chapter of *सुश्रुतसंहिता निदानस्थान*, this verse defines the normal physiological function and primary seat of *अपान वायु* [R1]. The author explains that *अपान*, residing in the *पक्वाशय*, naturally moves downward at the appropriate time to facilitate the proper excretion and elimination of *शकृत्*, *मूत्र*, *शुक्र*, *गर्भ*, and *आर्तव* [R1]. Understanding this normal downward faculty forms the basis for recognising pathological manifestations when this *समीरण* gets vitiated [R1, R2].

The Acharya deliberately pairs the seat of the large intestine with the active verb *कर्षति*, implying that the physiological expulsion of waste and reproductive elements is not a passive dripping, but an active, force-driven descent executed by the dynamic qualities of the wind [R1]. By grouping *गर्भ* and *आर्तव* alongside *शकृत्* and *मूत्र*, the text subtly hints that reproductive physiology and excretory mechanics share a singular anatomical driver, suggesting why disorders of elimination frequently manifest as gynaecological and seminal pathologies [R1]. Furthermore, the inclusion of the word *काले* acts as a crucial condition, warning that any disruption in the periodicity of this downward force directly precipitates retention or untimely evacuation, forming the foundational mechanism for subsequent systemic diseases [R1].

In this chapter of the सुश्रुतसंहिता focusing on the pathology of wind, the author explains the specific pathological consequences arising from the aggravation of specific sub-types of वायु [R1]. Specifically, when the व्यान and अपान vayu are aggravated, they produce severe and distressing diseases localized in the bladder and rectum [R1]. Contribution: Provides the exact etiological mechanism, tracing the root cause of these specific disorders directly to the combined aggravation of the Vyana and Apana sub-divisions of Vayu.

By specifically coupling the systemic circulation of *Vyana* with the downward elimination of *Apana*, the Acharya implies that the etiology of complex urinary and reproductive pathologies lies not in isolated local tissue failure, but in a synchronized neurovascular and kinetic breakdown within the lower pelvic cavity [R1]. The selection of the term *Ghoran* suggests that when these two specific sub-divisions of Vayu act in concert to derange the bladder and rectum, the resulting conditions—such as deep-seated *Prameha* and structural *Shukra dosha*—become exceptionally difficult to reverse due to the foundational nature of the channels involved [R1]. Furthermore, by designating these disorders as direct products of *Vyana-Apana prakopa*, the text hints at a hemodynamic and excretory cross-talk where systemic circulatory pressure directly impairs urinary concentration and seminal retention [R1].

आचार्य सुश्रुत employs the आत्मनेपद form 'कुरुते' to subtly intimate that the pathological modifications generated by aggravated Vayu are self-perpetuating, reflecting directly back upon the physiological integrity of the body without requiring external agency [R1]. By transitioning from general systemic provocation to the specific anatomical locus of the आमाशय, the author underscores the principle of 'स्थानसंश्रय' wherein a mobile dosha settling in a vulnerable receptacle inevitably triggers a cascade of site-specific symptoms such as vomiting [R1]. Furthermore, the employment of the emphatic particle 'हि' alongside the reiteration of the verb establishes an inescapable physiological certainty: whenever the wind is provoked within the gastric seat, upper gastrointestinal disturbances manifest as its mandatory corollary [R1].

पक्वाशयस्थः = located in the pakvashaya (colon) | मोहम् = delusion/loss of consciousness | मूर्च्छाम् = fainting | पिपासाम् = thirst | च = and | हृद्ग्रहम् = constriction/seizure in the heart | पार्श्ववेदनाम् = pain in the flanks | अन्त्रकूजम् = gurgling sound in the intestines | नाभौ = in the navel | शूलम् = sharp/colic pain | करोति = causes | च = and
Sentence meaning: Located in the pakvashaya, Vayu causes delusion, fainting, thirst, constriction in the heart, pain in the flanks, gurgling sound in the intestines, and also sharp pain in the navel.

In the context of describing the various pathological manifestations caused by aggravated Vata in the *Nidana Sthana* of the *Sushruta Samhita*, this verse details the specific symptoms that arise when *वायु* localizes in the *पक्वाशय* [R1]. The author intends to highlight that when the vitiated *समीरण* is situated in the large intestine, it disrupts physiological functions by producing systemic and localized distresses such as delusion, fainting, extreme thirst, cardiac constriction, flank pain, intestinal gurgling, and sharp colic pain in the navel region [R1].

आचार्य Sushruta strategically uses terms like मोहम् and मूर्च्छाम् while describing पक्वाशयस्थ वायु to hint at the profound neurological impact that lower-gut disturbances exert on the higher faculties through upward reflexive pathways [R1]. By juxtaposing localized abdominal signs like अन्त्रकूजम् and नाभिदेशशूलम् with distant cardiac and cerebral distress such as हृद्ग्रहम्, the author employs तंत्रयुक्ति (गुणार्थसंश्रय) to demonstrate that the Ruksha and Khara qualities of aggravated Vata in its primary seat can instantaneously compromise both circulatory and cognitive stability [R1]. Furthermore, the repetitive use of the connective particle च underscores the holistic and simultaneous disruption of multiple organ systems, revealing that a pathology originating in the colon is never confined to a single local symptom [R1].

Aggravated Vayu causes difficulty in urination and defecation, abdominal distension, pain in the sacral region, and impairment of the sense faculties in the ears and other organs.

In this verse from the *वातव्याधिदान* chapter of the *सुश्रुतसंहिता निदानस्थान*, the author elaborates on the specific pathological manifestations produced by aggravated *समीरण* (वात) [R1]. Continuing the description of its localized effects, the text explains that when *वात* is vitiated, it disrupts excretory functions, causing difficulty in passing urine and stool, along with abdominal distension (*आनाह*) and pain in the sacral region (*त्रिकवेदना*) [R1]. Furthermore, it impairs the functioning of the sense organs including the ears (*श्रोत्रादिष्विन्द्रियवध*), demonstrating how a localized *दोष* can produce diverse somatic and sensory disturbances [R1].

The Acharya intentionally links the obstruction of lower excretory pathways with the impairment of superior sensory faculties, hinting at the pervasive, upward-and-downward bidirectional turmoil characteristic of aggravated Vayu. By employing the term *इन्द्रियवध*, the author suggests that chronic or severe functional displacement of the mobile principle does not merely cause localized pain, but actively extinguishes the perceptive capacity of the sense organs by blocking their respective channels. The use of the prefix *सम्* in *समीरण* further implies that when the dynamic flow of Vayu is intensively agitated, it loses its normal physiological compliance and exerts a disruptive pressure across both somatic and neurological boundaries.

त्वक्स्थः वैवर्ण्यं स्फुरणं रौक्ष्यं सुप्तिं चुमुचुमायनम् निस्तोदनं त्वग्भेदं परिपोटनं च कुर्यात्।

त्वक्स्थः = located in the skin [R1] | वैवर्ण्यम् = discoloration [R1] | स्फुरणम् = throbbing [R1] | रौक्ष्यम् = dryness [R1] | सुप्तिम् = numbness [R1] | चुमुचुमायनम् = tingling sensation [R1] | निस्तोदनम् = pricking pain [R1] | त्वग्भेदम् = splitting or cracking of the skin [R1] | परिपोटनम् = bursting or breaking open of the skin [R1] | कुर्यात् = should cause [R1].

Located in the skin, [the aggravated Vata] should cause discoloration, throbbing, dryness, numbness, tingling sensation, pricking pain, splitting of the skin, and bursting open of the skin [R1].

In this chapter on the diagnosis of vatavyadhi within the Nidana Sthana of the Sushruta Samhita, the author delineates the specific symptoms manifested when aggravated Vata localizes in different bodily tissues [R1]. Specifically, when the vitiated dosha is seated in the skin (त्वक्स्थः), it produces distinct dermatological and sensory disturbances such as discoloration, dryness, numbness, tingling, and various forms of pain and cracking [R1]. Thus, the acharya intends to guide physicians in recognizing the precise site of vitiation based on these characteristic cutaneous signs [R1].

By employing specific terms such as रौक्ष्यम् and परिपोटनम्, आचार्य सुश्रुत intentionally signals how the dry, mobile, and cutting qualities of aggravated वातायु are directly expressed within the superficial coverings of the body [R1]. The structural progression of symptoms—starting from subtle sensory alterations like चुमुचुमायनम् and सुप्तिम् and culminating in macroscopic structural disruptions like त्वग्भेदम् and परिपोटनम्—reveals a deep clinical insight into the gradual, compounding deterioration caused by the dosha [R1]. Furthermore, the precise placement of the term त्वक्स्थः at the outset establishes a methodological blueprint, reminding the practitioner that the anatomical ashraya dictates the exact phenomenological presentation of a vatavyadhi long before it penetrates deeper structural layers [R1].

The blood-situated [fault] should produce painful lumps and ulcers, and thus the fat-situated [fault] should produce lumps with mild pain and without ulcers.

In this verse from the ग्रन्थिनिदान प्रकरण of सुश्रुतसंहिता निदानस्थान, the author explains the specific manifestations of the aggravated doshas based on their precise anatomical locations in the blood, muscles, and fat [R1], [R2]. When the doshas affect the blood and muscle tissues, they produce distinct lumps accompanied by pain and ulceration [R1]. Conversely, when localized in the fatty tissue, they cause lumps that are characterized by only mild pain and the absence of ulcers [R1]. Thus, the acharya highlights how the specific tissue site determines the unique clinical features of the lumps [R1].

By explicitly contrasting the acute, ulcerating pathology of the blood and muscle layers with the sluggish, non-ulcerative nature of the deeper fat layer, the आचार्य reveals a profound rule of tissue-depth: as the vitiated doshas travel inward from the surface vessels toward dense adipose tissue, the associated inflammation transitions from sharp, destructive tissue-breaking processes to dull, stagnant, and localized swellings. The precise deployment of terms denoting tissue residence (*रक्तगः*, *मांससंश्रितः*, *मेदःश्रितः*) demonstrates that the chronicity and destructive potential of a swelling are directly governed by the Ushna and Tikshna qualities encountering progressively denser, less circulating media [R1]. Thus, the verse acts as an anatomical diagnostic map, hinting that the clinician must look beyond the mere presence of a lump and evaluate its deep tissue-layer affinity to predict ulceration and pain severity [R1].

आचार्य सुश्रुत employs the prefix 'सम्' in 'सञ्चरति' alongside 'क्रमात्' to subtly reveal that the mobility of वायु is not a random, chaotic scattering, but a disciplined, sequential invasion of deep anatomical structures starting from the extremities and moving inward to the vital seats. By contrasting this ordered progression with the potential absolute pervasion ('व्याप्नुयाद्वा अखिलं देहम्'), the text hints at a dual clinical phenotype: either a localized, migrating affliction that mimics shifting joint and tissue pain, or a sudden, catastrophic systemic collapse where the all-pervading nature of the humor overwhelms the entire physical frame simultaneously. Furthermore, the inclusion of 'धातूँन्' alongside peripheral landmarks like hands, feet, and head implies that vitiated वायु bridges superficial motor structures with deep metabolic repositories, establishing that neurological and movement disorders inherently carry the potential to corrupt the fundamental tissue matrix of the human body.

पद: पित्तसमन्विते
Synonyms: पित्तयुक्ते, पित्तसंयुक्ते
Grammar: सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् सप्तमी एकवचनम् (समस्तपदम्: पित्तैन समन्वितः — पित्तसमन्वितः, तृतीया तत्पुरुषः समासः; पित्त — धातु: पित् | धात्वर्थ: तापे; समन्वित — धातु: सम् + अनु + इ | धात्वर्थ: मिलने / युक्ते)
धातु: इ | धात्वर्थ: गतौ / सम्बन्धने (to go, to join)
उपसर्ग: सम्, अनु — indicate complete and harmonious conjunction or association.
Contribution: Specifies the crucial synergistic dual-dosha condition (Vayu mixed with Pitta) that triggers specific thermal complications like burning and fainting.

आचार्य सुश्रुत intends to reveal through the word अमितान् किम्बहुना तन्त्रस्य व्याप्तिः that when the inherently mobile मारुतः invades the deeper अवयव, the resulting pathologies defy singular classification and multiply across channels [R1]. The prefix प्र in अवयवप्राप्तः signifies a deep, unhindered penetration into structural sites, transforming a localized kinetic disturbance into a systemic multi-organ crisis [R1]. By utilizing the term पित्तसमन्विते, the आचार्य covertly establishes that thermal aggravation is not merely a co-occurrence, but an active chemical combustion driven by Vayu's kinetic friction upon Pitta's latent Ushna quality, inevitably precipitating acute neurological collapse manifest as दाहसन्तापमूर्च्छाः [R1].

कफावृते तस्मिन्नेव शैत्यशोफगुरुत्वानि सूचीभिरिव निस्तोदः स्पर्शद्वेषः प्रसुप्तता (स्युः)

कफावृते = when covered by kapha | तस्मिन् = in that (vata) | एव = indeed | शैत्यशोफगुरुत्वानि = coldness, swelling, and heaviness [R1] | सूचीभिः = with needles | इव = like [R1] | निस्तोदः = pricking pain [R1] | स्पर्शद्वेषः = aversion to touch [R1] | प्रसुप्तता = numbness [R1] | 

When that (vata) is covered by kapha indeed, coldness, swelling, and heaviness, pricking pain like with needles, aversion to touch, and numbness (occur).

In the context of describing the various pathological manifestations caused by the obstruction of Vata by other doshas within the Nidana Sthana of the Sushruta Samhita, this verse details the specific clinical features that arise when Vata is enveloped by Kapha [R1]. The author intends to highlight that such an obstruction produces distinct physical signs characterized by the heavy, cold, and sluggish qualities inherent to Kapha, combined with the peculiar neurological symptoms of Vata [R1]. Consequently, the patient suffers from coldness, localized swelling, heaviness, a pricking pain resembling needles, aversion to physical touch, and a state of numbness [R1].

धातुः: स्वप् (शये) | धात्वर्थः: to sleep, to be numb [R1]
उपसर्गः: प्र — प्रकृष्टरूपेण (profoundly, completely)
Contribution: The abstract suffix 'तल्' along with the upasarga 'प्र' designates the complete loss of sensation or profound numbness in the affected part [R1].

The Acharya subtly underscores that when the mobile, subtle, and drying qualities of Vata are completely enveloped by the heavy, cold, and sluggish properties of Kapha, the typical dynamism of Vata is hindered, resulting in localized stasis [R1]. By employing the particle एव along with the locative form, the author implies that these specific sensory alterations do not manifest from a simple aggravation of either dosha alone, but specifically from their pathological entanglement where Kapha acts as an obstructive sheath [R1]. Furthermore, the imagery of needle pricking (सूचीभिरिव निस्तोदः) combined with deep-seated numbness (प्रसुप्तता) reveals a profound paradox where the channel is sluggish and cold, yet retains a sharp, localized nerve irritation beneath the surface [R1].

In the context of the classification of various disorders arising from the aggravation and localization of वायु in specific bodily locations and with different associations (निदानस्थान, वातावरणप्रकरण) [R1], this verse details the specific pathological symptoms resulting from combined doshic conditions. When मारुत is combined with शोणित, it produces the remaining पित्तविकाराः, and when प्राणवायु is enveloped by पित्त, specific symptoms such as छर्दि and दाह manifest [R1]. Thus, the author explains how the interaction of वात with शोणित or पित्त leads to distinct clinical manifestations in the body [R1].

The pairing of vomiting and burning sensation as direct outcomes of Prana's obstruction hints that when upward-moving Vata is trapped by hot Pitta, it forces a violent, retroperistaltic expulsion rather than normal downward or outward function [R1].

When Udana vayu is combined with Pitta and covered by Kapha, weakness, languor, drowsiness, discoloration, fainting, burning sensation, dizziness, and exhaustion arise.

In this chapter of the सुश्रुतसंहिता Nidana Sthana discussing the complications of vitiated vayu, this verse details the specific clinical features produced when the उदान वायु is simultaneously associated with पित्त and obstructed by कफ [R1]. The author's true intent is to highlight how this dual pathological involvement manifests as general debility, prostration, drowsiness, discoloration, alongside symptoms of burning and dizziness [R1]. Thus, the presence of these signs indicates the complex interplay of doshas specifically affecting the function and pathway of उदान वायु [R1].

By selecting the terms दौर्बल्य and सदनम्, the आचार्य reveals a deep understanding of how the heavy, obstructing nature of Kapha suppresses the expansive, dynamic quality of Udana, leading to an immediate collapse of physical vigor. The simultaneous presence of Pitta, indicated through terms like दाह and वैवर्ण्य, points to a complex thermal conflict where the cooling, heavy barriers of Kapha trap and intensify Pitta's heat within the upper channels of the body. Furthermore, the combination of neurological symptoms such as मूर्च्छा and भ्रम underscores how the upward-moving Vayu, when tangled with these dual doshas, disturbs cerebral circulation and sensory stability [R1].

Within the context of discussing the various pathological manifestations of obstructed Vayu in the Nidana Sthana of the सुश्रुतसंहिता, this verse details the specific clinical features produced when the समानवायु is afflicted by both कफ and पित्त [R1]. When covered by कफ, it causes symptoms such as absence of sweat, lack of horripilation, sluggish digestive fire, coldness, and stiffness [R1]. Simultaneously, when associated with पित्त, it gives rise to sweating, a burning sensation, internal heat, and fainting [R1].

The friction between heavy कफ-obstruction and sharp पित्त-reaction within the core of digestion creates paradoxical clinical states where systemic chill and internal burning coexist.

When the apana vayu is combined with pitta and covered by kapha, there occur increased feces and urine, horripilation, burning sensation, heat, and asrugdara (bleeding disorder).

In this verse from the वातावरण प्रकरण of सुश्रुतसंहिता निदानस्थान, आचार्य सुश्रुत describes the specific pathological manifestations that arise when अपानवायु is simultaneously associated with पित्त and obstructed by कफ [R1]. The author intends to explain that this complex morbid condition produces an excess of faeces and urine, horripilation, internal heat and burning sensations, along with असृग्दर (menorrhagia or abnormal uterine bleeding) [R1].

पद: एव
Synonyms: निश्चयेश, हि (indeed, certainly)
Grammar: अव्ययम्, अवधारणे (emphasizing particle)
धातु: none | धात्वर्थ: none
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Emphasizes certainty, leaving no doubt that these specific symptoms inevitably appear when Kapha envelops Vyana Vata.

The आचार्य implicitly reveals through the deployment of terms denoting heaviness and stability that the active, circulating nature of *Vyana Vata* is completely arrested by the dense, heavy, and cold qualities of *Kapha* [R1, R8]. By specifically noting the involvement of *asthi* and *parva*, the text underscores that this envelopment penetrates deep into the structural framework and joints of the body rather than remaining merely superficial [R1]. The choice of *chestastambha* further signals a profound loss of dynamic function, demonstrating that when the force responsible for all body movements is smothered by *Kapha*, physical freedom translates into complete rigidity [R1].

1st पाद- वायोः प्रकृतिभूतस्य
2nd पाद- व्यापन्नस्य च कोपनैः
3rd पाद- स्थानं कर्म च रोगांश्च
4th पाद- वद मे वदतां वर

9. रोगांश्च — सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् द्वितीया बहुवचनम् (पदान्तसहितः - रोगान् + च) [R1]

हे वदतां वर! प्रकृतिभूतस्य व्यापन्नस्य च वायोः कोपनैः (हेतुभिः) स्थानं कर्म च रोगान् च मे वद।

हे वदताम् = O best | वर = among speakers | प्रकृतिभूतस्य = of Vayu in its normal state | च = and | व्यापन्नस्य = of Vayu in its vitiated state | कोपनैः = by aggravating factors | वायोः = of Vayu | स्थानम् = the seat | कर्म = the function | च = and | रोगान् = diseases | च = and | मे = to me | वद = tell.

O best among speakers, tell to me the seat, the function, and the diseases of Vayu, both in its normal state and when vitiated by aggravating factors.

In this verse, situated at the beginning of the Nidana Sthana of the Sushruta Samhita, the disciple Sushruta asks his preceptor Dhanvantari to expound upon the fundamental nature of Vayu [R1]. The author intends for the student to understand the physiological seats and normal functions of Vayu in its balanced state, as well as its aggravating factors, pathological changes, and the specific diseases it causes when vitiated [R1, R2, R3]. This inquiry forms the foundational basis for diagnosing and treating the numerous disorders arising from the derangement of Vayu within the body [R1, R3].

धातु: none | धात्वर्थ: none

धातु: वृङ् (वरणे) | धात्वर्थ: to choose, to excel
उपसर्ग: none

By structuring his inquiry to address Vayu first in its pristine, natural baseline and subsequently in its pathological deviation, the Acharya establishes the fundamental Ayurvedic maxim that any clinical assessment of disease must be preceded by a thorough comprehension of physiological normalcy [R1]. The deliberate positioning of etiological factors alongside seats, functions, and resultant disorders hints at the clinician's imperative to trace every pathological manifestation backward to its specific root cause in order to formulate effective therapy [R1, R3]. Furthermore, addressing the preceptor as the foremost among speakers subtly underscores that the subtle dynamics of Vayu—being the primary mover of both body and cosmos—require an authoritative, master-level transmission rather than superficial memorization [R1, R4].

2nd पाद- मिथ्याऽऽहारविहारिणाम्
3rd पाद- रोगाध्वप्रमदामद्य-

6. च — अव्ययम् — समुच्चये (and)
7. अतिपीडनात् — सुबन्तः — नपुंसकलिङ्गम् पञ्चमी एकवचनम्
प्रायशः सुकुमाराणां मिथ्याऽऽहारविहारिणाम् रोगाध्वप्रमदामद्यव्यायामैः च अतिपीडनात् [R1]

प्रायशः = mostly [R1] | सुकुमाराणां = of tender persons [R1] | मिथ्याऽऽहारविहारिणाम् = of those who have improper diet and regimen [R1] | रोगाध्वप्रमदामद्यव्यायामैः = by disease, walking/travel, women, wine, and exercise [R1] | च = and [R1] | अतिपीडनात् = due to excessive affliction/overstraining [R1]

Mostly, due to the excessive affliction of tender persons—who indulge in improper diet and regimen—by disease, walking/travel, women, wine, and exercise [R1].

In the context of the Nidana Sthana of the सुश्रुतसंहिता, while detailing the causative factors of specific disorders, the author explains the specific etiology of वातरक्त [R1, R7]. The Acharya intends to convey that individuals who are of tender constitution and habitually consume improper diets and follow faulty regimens become susceptible [R1]. Specifically, excessive strain brought about by illness, long journeys, overindulgence in women, wine, and strenuous physical exercise acts as a primary catalyst for the aggravation of these humors [R1].

धातु: हॄ (हरणे) | धात्वर्थ: to take or to move / conduct
उपसर्ग: आ, वि (directional and distributive action)
Contribution: The compound highlights the causal etiology of contradictory diet and lifestyle choices as a direct trigger for pathogenesis [R1].

The enumeration of specific stressors like walking and women highlights an underlying somatic depletion that deprives the channels of protective unctuousness, thereby creating an immediate vulnerability to aggravated Vata [R1]. Furthermore, the syntactical placement of 'अतिपीडनात्' in the ablative case underscores a cumulative kinetic overload as the ultimate precipitating threshold, revealing that even normal physiological activities transform into pathology when pushed beyond the body's adaptive capacity [R1].

ऋतुसात्म्यविपर्यासात् स्नेहादीनां च विभ्रमात् अव्यवाये स्थूले तथा वातरक्तं प्रकुप्यति ।

ऋतुसात्म्यविपर्यासात् = due to the reversal of seasonal suitability | स्नेहादीनाम् = of oleation and others | च = and | विभ्रमात् = due to the disorder / improper administration | अव्यवाये = in lack of exercise / in non-separation | स्थूले = in an obese person | तथा = similarly | वातरक्तम् = the disease Vatarakta | प्रकुप्यति = gets aggravated |
Due to the reversal of seasonal suitability, and due to the disorder of oleation and others, similarly in non-exercise and in an obese person, Vatarakta gets aggravated.

In this verse from the वातरक्तनिदान प्रकरण of सुश्रुतसंहिता निदानस्थान, आचार्य सुश्रुत elucidates the specific etiological factors that provoke वातरक्त [R1]. The aggravation of the disease is triggered by the reversal of seasonal regimens and suitability (ऋतुसात्म्यविपर्यासात्), errors or irregularities in oleation and allied therapeutic procedures (स्नेहादीनां च विभ्रमात्), lack of physical exertion or coitus (अव्यवाये), and its particular predisposition in obese individuals (स्थूले) [R1]. Thus, improper lifestyle habits and faulty therapeutic management directly disturb the doshas to initiate the pathology of वातरक्त [R1].

हस्त्यश्वोष्ट्रैः अन्यैः च गच्छतः वायुः स्वैः कारणैः तीक्ष्णोष्णाम्लक्षारशाकादिभोज्यैः सन्तापाद्यैः भूयसा सेवितैः च कोपं यातः।

हस्त्यश्वोष्ट्रैः = by elephants, horses, and camels | अन्यैः = and by other (vehicles/animals) | च = and | गच्छतः = of one going (riding) | वायुः = the wind (Vayu) | स्वैः = by its own | कारणैः = causes | तीक्ष्णोष्णाम्लक्षारशाकादिभोज्यैः = by sharp, hot, sour, alkaline, vegetable, and other such foods | सन्तापाद्यैः = by heat and other (factors) | भूयसा = excessively | सेवितैः = indulged in | च = and | कोपम् = anger (aggravation) | यातः = has attained (becomes aggravated) [R1].

By riding elephants, horses, camels, and other (animals/vehicles), and by the excessive indulgence in its own causes, along with sharp, hot, sour, alkaline, and vegetable foods, as well as heat and other factors, the Vayu becomes aggravated [R1].

In the context of वातरक्तनिदान अध्याय of सुश्रुतसंहिता, आचार्य सुश्रुत explains the specific etiological factors responsible for the aggravation of वात in वातरक्त [R1]. The verse highlights that riding on elephants, horses, camels, and similar vehicles, along with the excessive use of sharp, hot, sour, alkaline, and specific vegetable foods as well as exposure to intense heat, directly provokes the वात दोष [R1]. Thus, these particular dietary indiscretions and physical strains act as primary catalysts in initiating the pathological process of the disease [R1].

चार्य सुश्रुत selects specific movement descriptors like riding elephants, horses, and camels to highlight how violent mechanical vibrations and uneven physical jarring act as direct physical catalysts for mobilizing aggravated Vayu. The explicit inclusion of both rigorous physical transit and heating, sharp dietary items reveals an underlying intent to show that Vatarakta pathogenesis requires a simultaneous assault of mechanical trauma and biochemical irritation. By emphasizing excessive indulgence through repetition, the Acharya hints that cumulative minor strains eventually cross a physiological threshold, transforming subtle doshic imbalance into a full-blown systemic pathology.

Blood quickly attains vitiation, and that (vitiated blood), going into the path of the wind, quickly obstructs it; that aggravated wind, due to the obstruction of its path, should excessively and quickly vitiate the intensely provoked blood.

In the context of वातरक्तनिदान अध्याय within सुश्रुतसंहिता निदानस्थान, आचार्य सुश्रुत explains the mutual vitiation of रक्त and वायु [R1]. When blood becomes vitiated quickly due to specific causative factors, it enters and obstructs the pathways of the wind [R1]. This obstruction further aggravates वायु, which in turn intensely vitiates the blood even more, creating a continuous pathological cycle [R1].

Grammar: सुबन्तः, नपुंसकलिङ्गम्, प्रथमा/द्वितीया एकवचनम् (क्तान्तम्)

पद: वायुना
Synonyms: वातेन, अनिलेन, मरुता
Grammar: सुबन्तः, पुंलिङ्गम्, तृतीया एकवचनम्
धातु: वा (गतौ गन्धने च) | धात्वर्थ: movement or blowing
उपसर्ग: न
Contribution: Highlights Vata as the active, dynamic agent responsible for initiating the pathology within the circulatory system [R1].

पद: दूषितेन
Synonyms: मलिनीकृतेन, प्रदुष्टेन, विकृतेन
Grammar: सुबन्तः, पुंलिङ्गम्, तृतीया एकवचनम् (क्तान्तम्)
धातु: दूष् (वैगुण्यकरणे) | धात्वर्थ: to spoil or vitiate
उपसर्ग: न
Contribution: Indicates that normal Vata is harmless; only the vitiated (pathological) state of Vata can corrupt the blood [R1].

पद: तत्प्राबल्यात्
Synonyms: तस्य प्राबल्यात्, मुख्यत्वात्
Grammar: सुबन्तः, नपुंसकलिङ्गम्, पञ्चमी एकवचनम् (षष्ठीतत्पुरुषसमासः)

उपसर्ग: प्र (आधिक्ये) | Contribution: Explains the naming convention; because Vata is dominant in the mixture, the disease is termed 'Vatarakta' [R1].

पद: उच्यते
Synonyms: कथ्यते, अभिधीयते, निगद्यते

Grammar: सुबन्तः, नपुंसकलिङ्गम्, प्रथमा/द्वितीया एकवचनम् (कर्मधारयसमासः / द्वन्द्वगर्भितः)

पद: तद्वत्

पद: दूषितेन
Synonyms: मलिनीकृतेन, प्रदुष्टेन
Grammar: सुबन्तः, नपुंसकलिङ्गम्, तृतीया एकवचनम् (क्तान्तम्)

उपसर्ग: न

पद: असृजा

Grammar: सुबन्तः, नपुंसकलिङ्गम्, तृतीया एकवचनम् (असृज्-शब्दः)
धातु: सृज् (विसर्गे) | धात्वर्थ: to emit or flow
उपसर्ग: न
Contribution: Designates blood explicitly in its instrumental form, highlighting its role as the physical medium saturated by doshas [R1].

पद: आक्तम्
Synonyms: व्याप्तम्, लिप्तम्, सम्बद्धम्
Grammar: सुबन्तः, नपुंसकलिङ्गम्, प्रथमा/द्वितीया एकवचनम् (क्तान्तम्)
धातु: अञ्ज् (व्यक्तायां वाचि रूपकयोः / सम्भक्तौ) | धात्वर्थ: to anoint, smear, or pervade
उपसर्ग: न
Contribution: Describes how Pitta and blood permeate each other completely, resulting in intense burning sensations characteristic of the Pitta variety [R1].

पद: श्लेष्मा
Synonyms: कफः, स्रोतः, श्लेष्मदोषः
Grammar: सुबन्तः, पुंलिङ्गम्, प्रथमा एकवचनम् (श्लेष्मन्-शब्दः)
धातु: श्लिष् (आश्लिष् - आलिङ्गने) | धात्वर्थ: to embrace, bind, or hold together
उपसर्ग: न
Contribution: Introduces Kapha as the third dosha involved in Vatarakta pathogenesis, bringing heaviness, coldness, and swelling [R1].

पद: दुष्टः
Synonyms: प्रकुपितः, विकृतः
Grammar: सुबन्तः, पुंलिङ्गम्, प्रथमा एकवचनम् (क्तान्तम्)
धातु: दुष् (वैगुण्यकरणे) | धात्वर्थ: to be spoiled or vitiated
उपसर्ग: न
Contribution: Specifies that Kapha must be in a pathological (vitiated) state to participate in this complex blood-disorder [R1].

पद: दूषितेन
Synonyms: मलिनीकृतेन, प्रदुष्टेन
Grammar: सुबन्तः, नपुंसकलिङ्गम्, तृतीया एकवचनम् (क्तान्तम्)
धातु: दूष् (वैगुण्यकरणे) | धात्वर्थ: to spoil or vitiate
उपसर्ग: न
Contribution: Reiterate the universal requirement of blood vitiation across all sub-types of Vatarakta [R1].

पद: असृजा
Synonyms: रक्तेन, शोणितेन
Grammar: सुबन्तः, नपुंसकलिङ्गम्, तृतीया एकवचनम् (असृज्-शब्दः)
धातु: सृज् (विसर्गे) | धात्वर्थ: to emit or flow
उपसर्ग: न
Contribution: Reaffirms blood as the essential tissue container that gets saturated by the heavy, sluggish Kapha dosha [R1].

पद: आक्तः
Synonyms: व्याप्तः, लिप्तः
Grammar: सुबन्तः, पुंलिङ्गम्, प्रथमा एकवचनम् (क्तान्तम्)
धातु: अञ्ज् (सम्भक्तौ) | धात्वर्थ: to anoint, smear, or pervade
उपसर्ग: न
Contribution: Denotes the thorough saturation of Kapha with blood, leading to chronic, cold, and numb manifestations of the disease [R1].

Using 'सम्पृक्तम्' for Vata and 'आक्तम्' for Pitta and Kapha reveals a subtle pathological distinction: Vata intimately interpenetrates the blood through dynamic movement, whereas Pitta and Kapha saturate and coat the pre-vitiated blood sluggishly like an anointment [R1]. The repetition of 'दूषितेन असृजा' underscores that Pitta and Kapha cannot corrupt pure blood on their own; they require the vascular bed to be pre-compromised, establishing blood as the mandatory substrate for all variants of the disease [R1].

2nd पाद- स्वापोपेतौ वातरक्तेन पादौ
3rd पाद- पित्तासृग्भ्यामुग्रदाहौ भवेता-
4th पाद- मत्यर्थोष्णौ रक्तशोफौ मृदू च

1. स्पर्शोद्विग्नौ — सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् प्रथमा द्विवचनम् [R1]

3. वातरक्तेन — सुबन्तः — नपुंसकलिङ्गम् तृतीया एकवचनम् [R1]
4. पादौ — सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् प्रथमा द्विवचनम् [R1]
5. पित्तासृग्भ्याम् — सुबन्तः — नपुंसकलिङ्गम् तृतीया द्विवचनम् [R1]
6. उग्रदाहौ — सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् प्रथमा द्विवचनम् [R1]
7. भवेताम् — तिङन्तः — विधिलिङ्, प्रथमपुरुषः, द्विवचनम् [R1]
8. अत्यर्थोष्णौ — सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् प्रथमा द्विवचनम् [R1]
9. रक्तशोफौ — सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् प्रथमा द्विवचनम् [R1]

11. च — अव्ययम् — समुच्चये (and) [R1]
वातरक्तेन पित्तासृग्भ्याम् च वातरक्ते पादौ स्पर्शोद्विग्नौ तोदभेदप्रशोषस्वापोपेतौ उग्रदाहौ अत्यर्थोष्णौ रक्तशोफौ मृदू भवेताम् ।

वातरक्तेन = by vatarakta (vayu and blood) [R1] | पित्तासृग्भ्याम् = by pitta and blood [R1] | च = and [R1] | पादौ = two feet [R1] | स्पर्शोद्विग्नौ = averse to touch [R1] | तोदभेदप्रशोषस्वापोपेतौ = endowed with pricking pain, splitting pain, excessive dryness, and numbness [R1] | उग्रदाहौ = having severe burning sensation [R1] | अत्यर्थोष्णौ = extremely hot [R1] | रक्तशोफौ = having red swelling [R1] | मृदू = soft [R1] | भवेताम् = should become [R1]

By vatarakta, pitta, and blood, the two feet become averse to touch, endowed with pricking pain, splitting pain, excessive dryness, and numbness, having severe burning sensation, extremely hot, having red swelling, and soft.

In this verse from the Vatarakta Nidana chapter of the Sushruta Samhita, the author describes the specific clinical features when vatarakta is predominantly influenced by pitta and blood [R1]. When pitta is vitiated and combined with tainted blood, the feet manifest symptoms such as aversion to touch, pricking and splitting pain, excessive dryness, and numbness [R1]. Additionally, the patient experiences severe burning, extreme heat, soft red swellings, and tenderness characteristic of pitta involvement [R1].

पद: स्पर्शोद्विग्नौ
Synonyms: स्पर्शद्वेषिणौ, असहमानौ
Grammar: सुबन्तः, पुंलिङ्गम्, प्रथमा, द्विवचनम् [R1]
धातु: स्पृश (स्पर्शने) | धात्वर्थः: to touch, contact
उपसर्ग: उद् (upwards, away) + विज् (भये - to fear, be agitated) -> उद्विग्न
Contribution: The compound highlights the extreme hypersensitivity where even a gentle touch becomes intolerable due to Vata and Pitta aggravation. [R1]

पद: तोदभेदप्रशोषस्वापोपेतौ
Synonyms: तोदेन भेदेन प्रशोषेण स्वापेन च उपेतौ
Grammar: सुबन्तः, पुंलिङ्गम्, प्रथमा, द्विवचनम् [R1]
धातु: तुद् (व्यथने) + घञ् (तोद), भिद् (विदारणे) + घञ् (भेद), शुष् (शोषणे) + घञ् (प्रशोष), स्वप् (शये) + घञ् (स्वाप), इ (गतौ) + क्त (उपेत) | धात्वर्थः: pricking, splitting, drying, sleeping/numbness, and endowed with
उपसर्ग: प्र (intensification) before शुष् -> प्रशोष; उप (near) before इ -> उपेत
Contribution: Enumerates multiple complex sensory manifestations showing the mixed involvement of Vata (pricking, splitting, dryness, numbness) in the pathogenesis. [R1]

पद: वातरक्तेन
Synonyms: वातेन दूषितेनासृजा
Grammar: सुबन्तः, नपुंसकलिङ्गम्, तृतीया, एकवचनम् [R1]
धातु: वा (गतिगन्धनयोः) + त, रञ्ज् (रागे) + क्त | धात्वर्थः: moving/blowing, and coloring/reddening
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Identifies the core causative pathological entity (Vata combined with blood) responsible for this specific clinical presentation. [R1]

पद: पादौ
Synonyms: चरणौ, पादप्रदेषौ
Grammar: सुबन्तः, पुंलिङ्गम्, प्रथमा, द्विवचनम् [R1]

उपसर्ग: none

पद: पित्तासृग्भ्याम्

धातु: तप् (दाहे) + क (पित्त), सृज् (विसर्गे) + क्निप् (असृक्) | धात्वर्थः: to heat, to create/discharge
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Denotes the co-involvement of Pitta and blood which adds specific inflammatory and burning features to the condition. [R1]

पद: उग्रदाहौ
Synonyms: तीक्ष्णसन्तप्तावौ, प्रकृष्टदाहौ
Grammar: सुबन्तः, पुंलिङ्गम्, प्रथमा, द्विवचनम् [R1]
धातु: उग्र (इञ् - गतौ कान्तौ वा), दह् (भस्मीकरणे) + घञ् | धात्वर्थः: terrible/severe, and burning
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: The adjective 'उग्र' emphasizes the intensity of the burning sensation caused by the hot potency of Pitta and vitiated blood. [R1]

पद: भवेताम्
Synonyms: स्युः, जायेताम्
Grammar: तिङन्तः, विधिलिङ्, प्रथमपुरुषः, द्विवचनम् [R1]
धातु: भू (सत्तायाम्) | धात्वर्थः: to become, to exist
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: The potential mood (विधिलिङ्) indicates the characteristic manifestation of symptoms that naturally arise under this specific pathological combination. [R1]

पद: अत्यर्थोष्णौ
Synonyms: अतीवोष्णौ, अतितापनौ

धातु: उष् (दाहे) + न | धात्वर्थः: to burn, to be hot
उपसर्ग: अति (excessive) prefixed to अर्थ + उष्ण
Contribution: Expresses the extreme degree of localized temperature elevation due to the thermal attributes of Pitta and rakta. [R1]

पद: रक्तशोफौ
Synonyms: रक्तेन सहिते शोफे ययोः तौ
Grammar: सुबन्तः, पुंलिङ्गम्, प्रथमा, द्विवचनम् [R1]
धातु: रञ्ज् (रागे) + क्त (रक्त), शुफ् (उच्छूनत्वे) + घञ् (शोफ) | धात्वर्थः: to color/redden, and to swell
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Connects the swelling with a distinct red coloration, pointing to the involvement of Rakta dhatu in the inflammatory swelling. [R1]

पद: मृदू
Synonyms: कोमलौ, असान्द्रौ
Grammar: सुबन्तः, पुंलिङ्गम्, प्रथमा, द्विवचनम् [R1]
धातु: मृद् (विक्षोदे) + कु | धात्वर्थः: to grind, to soften, to be tender
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Distinguishes the softness of the swelling caused by Pitta and blood from the hard or stable swellings seen in other variants. [R1]

पद: च
Synonyms: तथा, अपि
Grammar: अव्ययम्, समुच्चये (and) [R1]
धातु: none | धात्वर्थः: connective particle
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Links the multiple symptoms and causative factors together, indicating that all these signs occur in conjunction. [R1]

The pairing of 'स्पर्शोद्विग्नौ' with 'मृदू' highlights that Pitta and Rakta impart a vulnerable, yielding texture to the swelling, making the tissue acutely sensitive to mechanical pressure unlike the hard, stable masses seen in pure Vata or Kapha dominance [R1]. By deliberately employing both 'उग्रदाहौ' and 'अत्यर्थोष्णौ', the Acharya underscores the dual mechanism of localized thermal aggravation—where the inherent Ushna guna of Pitta is intensely amplified by the circulating Ushna and Tikshna properties of vitiated blood [R1].

2. श्वेतशीतौ — सुबन्तः — पुंलिङ्गम् द्वितीया द्विवचनम्

In the context of explaining the manifestations and spread of rat poison (आखुविष) within the Nidana Sthana of the Sushruta Samhita, the author describes how the aggravated poison behaves [R1]. Just like an enraged snake venom, this toxin typically originates or settles at the base of the feet, and sometimes at the hands [R1]. From there, it actively spreads and pervades throughout the entire body [R1].

भिषजाम् = of physicians | वरः = the best | तस्य = his | तत् = that | वचनम् = speech | श्रुत्वा = having heard | एषः = this | भगवान् = revered | स्वयम्भूः = self-born | वायुः = Vayu (wind) | इति = thus | अभिशब्दितः = called | प्राब्रवीत् = spoke [R1]

The best of physicians, having heard that speech of his, spoke, having called this revered [Vayu] as self-born Vayu [R1].

In the context of the वातव्याधिनिदान प्रकरण within the निदानस्थान of the सुश्रुतसंहिता, when the disciple inquires about the nature and pathologies of वायु, the preceptor — the best among physicians — responds by identifying the revered वायु as स्वयम्भू (self-born) [R1, R2]. The author's true intent here is to establish the supreme, fundamental, and autonomous status of वायु before detailing its specific morbid manifestations and diseases [R2, R7].

In the context of diagnosing the prognosis of vata-blood disorders within the Nidana Sthana of the सुश्रुतसंहिता, Acharya Sushruta explains the severity determined by the involvement of channels [R1]. When the vitiated मारुतः pervades all the धमनीः, the condition becomes असाध्यम्, whereas the same condition lasting for a full year is regarded as याप्यम् [R1]. Thus, the extensive spread across bodily channels serves as a critical indicator of incurability or chronicity in these pathological states [R1].

Acharya Sushruta utilizes this verse to reveal a profound principle of systemic pathology where anatomical saturation dictates prognosis, signaling that when an aggravated factor completely occupies all dynamic channels, localized disease transforms into a generalized, deep-seated crisis [R1]. The specific mention of a one-year threshold as manageable (*याप्य*) rather than completely hopeless implies that time acts as a structural consolidator of chronicity, allowing palliative containment before the pathology reaches absolute structural inflexibility [R1]. By focusing on the pervasive movement through all *धमनी*, the Acharya subtly instructs the physician to look beyond mere surface symptoms and evaluate the degree of channel occlusion, as the total usurpation of circulatory pathways by *मारुत* strips the body of its self-repairing elasticity [R1].

Within the context of Vata Vyadhi pathology in the Nidana Sthana, when the aggravated Vayu completely pervades and moves swiftly through the channels, it forcefully jerks the entire body [R1, R2]. Because of this repeated convulsive jerking (आक्षेप) of the limbs and body, the आचार्य Sushruta designates this specific clinical condition as आक्षेपक [R1].

By repeating the adverb मुहुर्मुहुः three times in a single verse, the आचार्य emphasizes the intrinsically intermittent, paroxysmal, and unpredictable cadence of Vata-driven crises. This relentless reiteration underscores the fundamental dynamic of आशुकारी and चरस्वभाव attributes of the wind, revealing that the true terror of आक्षेपक lies not in a singular spasm, but in its unyielding, repetitive assault on the somatic frame [R1, R2]. Furthermore, by grounding the disease nomenclature directly in the mechanical phenomenon of the body being cast or jerked (आक्षेपात्), the आचार्य signals that the clinical definition of a disorder must inherently mirror its most disruptive pathomechanical sign.

In this verse from the Apatanaka-prakarana of the Nidana Sthana in Sushruta Samhita, the author describes the specific clinical features of दण्डापतानक (Dandapatanaka), a severe type of vata-induced convulsive disorder. Vayu causing this condition renders the entire body of the patient rigid and straight like a staff (दण्डवत् स्तम्भयति), while simultaneously producing severe lockjaw (हनुग्रह). Consequently, the patient experiences great difficulty in consuming food [R1].

The juxtaposition of 'हनुग्रह' with the act of partaking in food through 'कृच्छ्र' subtly signals a vital obstruction to the downward-moving and entry pathways of sustenance, pointing to an imminent threat to life where structural rigidity cripples the fundamental physiological intake of nutrition.

यः तु धनुस्तुल्यं नमेत्, सः अङ्गुलीगुल्फजठरहृद्वक्षोगलसंश्रितः धनुःस्तम्भसञ्ज्ञकः।
Indeed, who bends like a bow, that condition located in the fingers, ankles, abdomen, heart, chest, and throat is called Dhanurstambha.

In the context of the classification of vata-induced major convulsive disorders (*आतानक* / *अपतानक*) within the *निदानस्थान* of सुश्रुतसंहिता, the author defines the specific clinical condition known as *धनुःस्तम्भ* [R1]. When aggravated *वायु* causes the patient's body to curve and bend uniformly like a drawn bow, the condition is termed *धनुःस्तम्भ* [R1]. This disease specifically manifests across multiple critical anatomical sites including the fingers, ankles, abdomen, heart, chest, and throat [R1].

धातु: धन्व् (गतौ) → धनुस् | स्तभ् (चुरादिः / स्वादिः - स्तम्भे) → स्तम्भ | सम् + ज्ञा (ज्ञाने) → सञ्ज्ञा [R1]
उपसर्ग: सम्
Contribution: Designates the clinical entity by its classic eponymous title, signifying a rigid bow-like posture.

पद: अङ्गुलीगुल्फजठरहृद्वक्षोगलसंश्रितः
Synonyms: अङ्गुध्यात्मन्युपस्थितादिः
Grammar: समासः (द्वन्द्वसमासः - अङ्गुली च गुल्फश्च जठरं च हृत् च वक्षः च गलश्च = अङ्गुलीगुल्फजठरहृद्वक्षोगलाः, तैः संश्रितः = तृतीयातत्पुरुषः); पुंलिङ्गम्, प्रथमा, एकवचनम् [R1]
धातु: श्रि (सेवायाम्) → संश्रित [R1]
उपसर्ग: सम्
Contribution: Exhaustively maps out the specific anatomical loci involved in the affliction, indicating widespread muscular and tendinous spasm.

By choosing the word धनुस्तुल्यम् to describe the physical curvature, the आचार्य implies a profound mechanical analogy where the human spine and extremities behave like an overtightened wooden bow under extreme tension, revealing the immense elastic potential stored within the contracted soft tissues. The inclusion of multiple specific sites ranging from peripheral extremities like अङ्गुली and गुल्फ to vital core regions like जठर, हृत्, वक्षस्, and गल demonstrates that the pathological वायु does not merely affect isolated joints, but creates a synchronous, systemic lock across the entire musculoskeletal axis. Through the precise use of the term संश्रितः, the text hints that the condition is deeply rooted in the structural matrix of the body rather than being a superficial muscular twitch, underscoring the severity of the underlying neuromuscular crisis.

वेगवान् = powerful | अनिलो = wind/Vata [R1] | यदा = when [R1] | स्नायुप्रतानम् = network of tendons/ligaments [R1] | आक्षिपति = agitates/pulls [R1] | विष्टब्धाक्षः = having fixed/stiff eyes [R1] | स्तब्धहनुः = having a stiff jaw [R1] | भग्नपार्श्वः = having broken/painful sides (flanks) [R1] | कफम् = phlegm/Kapha [R1] | वमन् = vomiting [R1]

When the powerful wind agitates the network of tendons, he (the patient) has fixed eyes, a stiff jaw, broken sides, and is vomiting phlegm.

In the context of the description of various forms of 𝙑āṭa-vyādhi within the *Nidāna Sthāna* of the *Suśruta Saṁhitā*, this verse describes the specific clinical presentation when aggravated *Vāta* affects the ligaments and tendons (*snāyu-pratāna*) [R1]. The author intends to highlight the severe somatic distress characterized by ocular fixation, mandibular rigidity, flank pain, and the expulsion of *Kapha* [R1], which subsequently leads to the manifestation of *Bāhyāyāma* [R2].

When a human being bends inwards like a bow, then the strong wind (vata) causes inward bending of this person.

In the context of वातव्याधि (specifically अपतानक) within the निदानस्थान of सुश्रुतसंहिता, आचार्य सुश्रुत describes the pathological manifestation of अभ्यन्तरायाम [R1, R8]. When the aggravated and powerful मारुत (वात) afflicts the internal स्नायुप्रतान, it forces the patient's body to curve forward or inward like a bent bow [R1, R3]. This intended meaning highlights how aggravated wind produces specific postural distortions in the body [R1, R6].

By selecting the term बली to describe the wind, the text implies an irresistible, forceful contraction that overpowers the natural tone of the internal soft tissues and ligaments [R1, R3]. The choice of the reflective आत्मनेपद form कुरुते further underscores how the body itself is involuntarily compelled to execute this pathological posture from within, driven entirely by the deep-seated force of the vitiated dosha [R1, R6].

When the aggravated Vata localises within the network of external tendons (बाह्यस्नायुप्रतान), it induces an external bending of the body along with a crushing or breaking sensation in the chest, waist, and thighs [R1]. Wise physicians declare this specific manifestation to be incurable (असाध्य) due to its profound disruption of the structural tendons and deep-seated affliction [R1].

Furthermore, by framing the prognosis through the collective authority of बुधाः, the आचार्य subtly cautions the physician against futile therapeutic interventions in conditions where the deep structural network has suffered irreversible physical shattering.

आचार्य सुश्रुत employs the reiteration of वायुः alongside terms like केवलः and कफपित्तान्वितः to subtly underscore that while complex pathological mixtures (संसर्ग) drive many convulsive disorders, pure unalloyed vata or dual-dosha involvement can independently manifest identical motor disturbances [R1]. By designating the trauma-induced variety as चतुर्थम् ("fourth"), the text establishes a distinct nosological category that bypasses traditional internal doshic provocation, pointing instead to a structural or physical disruption of the channels (स्रोतस्) and vital tissues [R1, R8]. The use of the particle तु marks a deliberate shift from spontaneous internal pathologies to externally triggered (अभिघातज) conditions, hinting that mechanical injury directly incites localized vata aggravation without requiring a protracted internal pathogenesis [R1, R8].

यः गर्भपातनिमित्तः शोणितातिस्रावात् अभिघातनिमित्तः च अपतानकः न सिध्यति।

यः = which [R1] | गर्भपातनिमित्तः = caused by abortion [R1] | शोणितातिस्रावात् = from excessive bleeding [R1] | अभिघातनिमित्तः = and caused by trauma / injury [R1] | च = and [R1] | अपतानकः = apatānaka (type of vatavyadhi) [R1] | न = not [R1] | सिध्यति = succeeds / is curable [R1]

Which apatānaka, caused by abortion, from excessive bleeding, and caused by trauma, is not curable.

In the context of the classification and prognosis of वातव्याधि in सुश्रुतसंहिता निदानस्थान अध्याय १, आचार्य सुश्रुत specifies the incurability of certain severe conditions [R1]. Specifically, when अपतानक arises due to specific etiological factors involving severe tissue depletion and trauma — namely गर्भपात (abortion), शोणितातिस्रवा (excessive hemorrhage), and अभिघात (physical injury) — it becomes असाध्य (incurable) [R1]. This verse highlights the grave prognosis of अपतानक when complicated by profound blood loss and traumatic injury, rendering treatment ineffective [R1].

By specifically linking अपतानक to गर्भपात and शोणितातिस्रवा, the आचार्य hints that profound dhatu-kshaya and the resulting absolute vacuum in the channels create an uncontrollable, empty-vessel (धातुक्षयजनित) state of वायु that completely resists palliative or nourishing therapies [R1]. The repeated use of the conjunction च emphasizes that whether the vital fluid is lost via internal depletion (abortion or hemorrhage) or external expulsion (trauma), the resulting vulnerability of the deep channels makes the nervous system's collapse irreversible [R1, R7].

सर्वेषाम् = of all | एव = indeed | सर्वात्मा = the soul of all | सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः = bowed to by all worlds | स्वातन्त्र्यात् = because of independence | नित्यभावात् = because of eternal existence | सर्वगत्वात् = because of being all-pervading | तथा = and / likewise | एव = indeed | च = and [R1]

Because of independence, because of eternal existence, and likewise indeed because of being all-pervading, he is indeed the soul of all and bowed to by all worlds [R1].

In the first chapter of सुश्रुतसंहिता निदानस्थान, while describing the paramount nature of वात, आचार्य सुश्रुत establishes its supreme cosmic status [R1]. Because वात possesses absolute independence, eternal existence, and an all-pervading nature, it is recognized as the soul of all beings and is universally revered by all worlds [R1]. This verse emphasizes that वायु is not merely a bodily humor, but the fundamental, omnipresent principle governing the universe [R1].

By anchoring the description of वात with absolute terms like स्वातन्त्र्य and नित्यभाव, the आचार्य hints that therapeutic management of conditions rooted in this dosha requires profound patience, as its deep-seated nature resists straightforward pacification [R1]. The causal triad of independence, eternity, and omnipresence serves as the underlying justification for why vitiated वात can instantaneously disrupt every tissue and channel without depending on other doshas for initiation [R1]. Furthermore, by designating it as सर्वात्मा and सर्वलोकनमस्कृत, the text subtly prepares the physician to view treatment not merely as mechanical mitigation of symptoms, but as a holistic restoration of the foundational life-force governing the entire organism [R1].

यदा = when | मातरिश्वा = the wind (Vayu) | अत्यर्थम् = excessively | प्रकुपितः = aggravated | अधोगमाः = going downwards | सतिर्यग्गाः = and going obliquely | ऊर्ध्वदेहगाः = and going to the upper body | धमनीः = the dhamanis (channels) | प्रपद्यते = enters |

When the excessively aggravated wind, going downwards, obliquely, and to the upper body, enters the dhamanis.

In the context of the Apatandhaka and Pakshaghata chapter within the Nidana Sthana of the Sushruta Samhita, this verse describes the core pathomechanism of hemiplegia [R1]. The author explains that when the wind (मातरिश्वा) becomes excessively aggravated, it enters all the channels (धमनीः) throughout the body—moving downwards, obliquely, and towards the upper body [R1]. This widespread invasion of the aggravated Vayu into the circulatory and nervous pathways sets the stage for the specific loss of bodily function characteristic of पक्षाघात [R1].

By employing the term मातरिश्वा instead of the standard word वायुः, the Acharya invokes the elemental and all-pervading kinetic fury akin to cosmic wind, signaling that the vitiating force possesses an overwhelming, uncontainable momentum [R1]. Furthermore, the employment of the prefix in प्रपद्यते underscores that this is not a gentle or gradual seepage, but a violent, total usurpation of the dhamanis that instantly destabilizes the structural integrity of the body's functional axes [R1].

Best among physicians call that indeed as pakshaghata, which loosening the ligamentous bindings of the joints of one side of the body, strikes that side.

In the context of वातव्याधिचिकित्सा within the निदानस्थान of सुश्रुतसंहिता, when the aggravated वायु (मातरिश्वा) enters and affects half of the body, expert physicians define this specific condition as पक्षाघात [R1]. The author intends to describe how the vitiated 
वात strikes one half of the body by loosening the joint connections (सन्धिबन्धान् विमोक्षयन्), thereby causing loss of function on that side [R1]. This verse clearly establishes the core clinical definition and mechanism of पक्षाघात resulting from aggravated 
वातप्रकोप [R1].

By choosing the term सन्धिबन्धान् विमोक्षयन्, आचार्य सुश्रुत reveals that the pathophysiology of पक्षाघात is not merely a loss of motor control, but a structural loosening and functional failure of the joint capsules and ligaments caused by the dry and mobile qualities of aggravated वायु [R1]. The prefix वि in विमोक्षयन् hints at a thorough and forcible decoupling of the structural integrity holding the limbs together, distinguishing this deep-seated articular breakdown from superficial muscular weakness [R1]. Furthermore, by invoking the collective consensus of भिषग्वराः, the author emphasizes that true expertise in diagnosis relies on recognizing this deep structural compromise of the joints rather than merely observing the outward paralysis of movement [R1].
