आचार्य सुश्रुत reveals a profound counter-intuitive prognostic principle here, where a pure, unadulterated single-dosha condition (शुद्धवातहतम्) is paradoxically deemed harder to treat than a combined one, because unmitigated Vata possesses extreme dry and subtle qualities that deeply entrench themselves in the channels without a secondary dosha to provide bulk or localization [R1]. The transition to a *samsrishta* state, involving another dosha like Pitta or Kapha, introduces dual-pathology signs that paradoxically make the disease more approachable and responsive to targeted dual-therapy interventions [R1]. Furthermore, by designating the *kshaya*-induced variety as strictly incurable (*असाध्यम्*), the Acharya implies that functional derangement driven by dynamic doshic vitiation allows room for medical reversal, whereas structural depletion of bodily tissues (*धातुक्षय*) represents an irreversible deficit that no amount of therapeutic management can reconstruct [R1].

Aggravated that Vayu would move upwards from its own place, and afflicts the heart, head, and temples, and causes convulsions in the body parts and bends them.

Within the context of the vatavyadhi-prakarana of the Nidana Sthana, Acharya Sushruta describes the severe clinical manifestations produced when aggravated Vayu moves upward from its normal site [R1, R4]. Such an upward-coursing Vayu afflicts critical upper body centers including the heart, head, and temples, while simultaneously causing convulsions and abnormal bending of the bodily limbs [R1]. These symptoms signify a profound pathological disturbance driven by the aggravated principle as it surges through the upper pathways of the body [R4].

When the heart is free, (he) becomes normal; indeed, when it is obstructed, (he) faints; this should be known as apatantraka caused by vata associated with kapha. [R1]

In the context of diagnosing the types of disorders arising from obstruction in the channels within the Nidana Sthana of Sushruta Samhita, this verse defines the core mechanism of अपतन्त्रक [R1]. When the heart (हृदय), which serves as the seat of consciousness and prana, is free from obstruction, the patient remains normal and conscious [R1]. However, when it becomes covered or obstructed by aggravated vata combined with kapha, the patient loses consciousness and faints, presenting the definitive clinical picture of अपतन्त्रक [R1].

By utilizing the emphatic particle and specific prepositional prefixes, the author underscores that the pathology of manya stambha does not arise from Vata vitiation alone, but specifically from its complete, physical entrapment by Kapha within the cervical channels [R1]. This implies that static postures and downward or strained gazes act synergistically with sluggish phlegm to anchor and immobilize the mobile nature of Vata, converting a systemic circulatory disturbance into a rigid, localized structural deficit [R1].

Excessively speaking loudly, or eating hard things, of one laughing, of one yawning, from a heavy burden, and also from an uneven bed.

In this verse from the *Nidāna Sthāna* of the *Suśruta Saṁhitā*, the author highlights specific physical activities and postural strains that provoke an upward-moving aggravated wind (*वायु*) in the pathogenesis of conditions like *मन्यास्तम्भ* and *अर्दित* [R1, R5]. Actions involving excessive loud speaking, chewing hard foods, laughing, yawning, lifting heavy burdens, or maintaining an uneven sleeping posture act as precipitating causes for this disorder [R1]. The author's true intent is to identify these everyday physical overexertions as direct etiological factors that disturb the bodily channels and lead to facial paralysis and neck stiffness [R1, R5].

उपसर्ग: वि (विशेषेण / विपरीतार्थे)
Contribution: Denotes an uneven or awkward physical posture that misaligns the body structures.

पद: शयनात्
Synonyms: शय्यातः, स्वापात्
Grammar: सुबन्तः, पुंलिङ्गम्, पञ्चमी एकवचनम् [R1]

पद: अपि
Synonyms: च, अप्यर्थे
Grammar: अव्ययम् (सम्भാവने / समुच्चये) [R1]
धातु: आप् (व्याप्तौ) | धात्वर्थ: reaching or encompassing
उपसर्ग: None
Contribution: Inclusive particle that aggregates these miscellaneous physical activities as secondary causes of Ardita.

Acharya Sushruta hints that everyday mechanical overexertions and postural indiscretions serve as sudden triggers that displace the vital upward-moving wind (*वायु*) toward the head and neck region [R2, R5]. By pairing vocal and oral strains like excessive loud speaking and chewing hard foods with involuntary or forced muscular actions like laughing and yawning, the author reveals how minor physical stressors break the functional equilibrium of local channels (*स्रोतस्*) [R2, R4]. Furthermore, the inclusion of external stresses such as heavy loads and uneven resting postures exposes the subtle vulnerability of the skeletal alignment, demonstrating that structural misalignments directly provoke localized neural and muscular distress (*मन्यास्तम्भ* and *अर्दित*) [R5, R7].

अतः शिरोनासौष्ठचिबुकललाटेक्षणसन्धिगः अनिलः वक्त्रम् अर्दयित्वा अर्दितं जनयति [R1]

Therefore, the wind, having reached the joints of the head, nose, lips, chin, forehead, and eyes, and having afflicted the face, produces Ardita.

In this context of Nidana Sthana discussing Vata-related disorders, the author explains the pathogenesis of the disease Ardita [R1]. When aggravated Vata localizes in the vulnerable joints of the head, nose, lips, chin, forehead, and eyes, it severely afflicts the face [R1]. By causing this affliction and distortion in the facial structure, it successfully produces the condition known as अर्दितम् [R1].

By employing the compound term 'शिरोनासौष्ठचिबुकललाटेक्षणसन्धिगः', the आचार्य hints that अर्दितम् is fundamentally a disorder of multiple interconnected anatomical junctions (*संधि*), suggesting that the aggravated वायु exploits these weak points to simultaneously compromise sensory and motor functions of the entire face [R1]. The use of the causative gerund 'अर्दयित्वा' implies that वायु does not merely occupy the space, but actively torments and twists the soft tissues and channels, directly mirroring how a similar mechanism of drying and contracting channels leads to conditions like अवबाहुकम् [R2] and गृध्रसी [R8]. Furthermore, the formulation 'अर्दितं जनयत्यतः' establishes a direct etiological continuity from the mechanical overexertions mentioned previously (such as laughing or heavy lifting) to the sudden, violent manifestation of facial distortion, reminding the practitioner that structural trauma and dynamic over-extension are the primary triggers for this affliction [R1].

This [Vayu] is the cause of the maintenance, origin, and destruction of beings, unmanifest, having manifest actions, and dry, cold, light, and rough.

In this verse from the *Vatavyadhinidana* chapter of the Sushruta Samhita Nidana Sthana, the author describes the fundamental cosmic and physical nature of वात (*Vayu*) [R7]. It establishes that वात (*Vayu*) is the ultimate cause behind the creation, maintenance, and destruction of all living beings, operating as an unmanifest force while simultaneously displaying manifest actions [R1]. Furthermore, it highlights the inherent physical attributes of वात (*Vayu*), characterizing it as dry (रूक्ष), cold (शीत), light (लघु), and rough (खर) [R1].

By coupling cosmic agency (स्थित्युत्पत्तिविनाशेषु कारणम्) directly with elemental physical properties (रूक्ष, शीत, लघु, खर), the text subtly establishes an unbroken continuum between universal macrocosmic forces and the microscopic, tactile realities of somatic imbalance.

In the context of the description of अर्दितरोग (facial paralysis) within the निदानस्थान of the सुश्रुतसंहिता, the author elaborates the specific clinical manifestations caused by the vitiated and localized अनिल [R1, R4]. When the aggravated wind afflicts the region, it results in the twisting of half of the face, turning of the neck, trembling of the head, impediment of speech, and various structural abnormalities in the eyes and other facial parts [R1, R4]. These signs collectively characterize the advanced symptomatic presentation of अर्दित [R4].

By employing the term त्वचि, आचार्य सुश्रुत intentionally limits the superficial spatial domain of the vayu's initial manifestation, hinting that the pathology begins in the outermost cutaneous layers before penetrating deeper structural elements [R1]. The use of the prefix प्र in प्राहुः coupled with व्याधिविशारदाः implies that the recognition of अर्दितम् requires seasoned clinical acumen rather than mere surface observation, as the subtle interplay of स्वापः and स्तोदः marks a distinct stage of vata vitiation [R1]. Furthermore, the precise pairing of ऊर्ध्वम् with मन्याहनुग्रहः reveals the आचार्य's underlying mechanical insight that an upward-coursing wind specifically seizes the upper body's structural axis, transforming a general neurological disturbance into a localized facial and cervical crisis [R1, R6].

Of the emaciated person, of the one whose eyes are unblinking, of the one who speaks with slurred speech, and of the one who is trembling, the severely three-year-old arditam disease is not curable.

In the context of diagnosing and prognosticating the vata-related disorders in the Nidana Sthana of the सुश्रुतसंहिता, the author outlines the poor prognosis of अर्दित (facial palsy) [R1, R5]. When the condition is chronic—persisting for three years—and is accompanied by severe complications and specific signs such as extreme emaciation, unblinking eyes, continuous and slurred speech, and trembling, it becomes incurable [R1]. Thus, the presence of these advanced clinical features along with chronicity signifies an unsaveable, incurable state of the disease [R1].

The choice of terms describing continuous speech impediment and violent tremors exposes an advanced stage where aggravated वायु has deeply invaded the vital channels of the head, completely destroying the physiological resilience needed for therapeutic reversal.

In the context of defining the various distinct manifestations of Vata disorders within the निदानस्थान of the सुश्रुतसंहिता, the author characterizes the specific disease known as गृध्रसी [R1]. When the vital tendon (कण्डरा) originating from the heel and toes becomes vitiated and afflicted by the aggravated अनिल, it obstructs the free forward movement and extension of the entire leg [R1]. This pathological restriction and stiffness caused by the afflicted tendon is precisely recognized by experts as the condition termed गृध्रसी [R1].

When vayu located in the hip agitates the tendon of the thigh, then the person becomes lame; and due to the impairment of both thighs, [he becomes] a cripple.

In the context of the vatavyadhi chapter within the Nidana Sthana of the Sushruta Samhita, the author explains the specific locomotor impairments caused by vitiated vayu affecting the lower limbs [R1]. When the aggravated vayu gets localized in the hip region and forcefully affects the tendon of a single thigh, it results in lameness, rendering the person खञ्ज [R1]. However, when both thighs are impaired by the affliction of vayu, the individual completely loses lower limb mobility and becomes crippled, known as पङ्गु [R1]. The intended meaning of the author is that the pathological action of vayu on the tendons of the hip and thighs directly disturbs walking ability and leads to these distinct conditions of disability [R1].

Furthermore, the use of the potential mood verb आदिशेत् conveys that the physician must look beyond transient symptoms and deliberately classify this clinical picture as a distinct, independent disease entity rather than dismissing it as a generic secondary complaint [R1].

In the context of the vata vyadhi nidana within the सुश्रुतसंहिता निदानस्थान, the author explains the specific manifestation and etiology of a localized condition known as पादहर्ष [R1]. When a person experiences a tingling sensation accompanied by a feeling of numbness or stiffness (प्रसुप्तवत्) in both feet, it is clinically identified as पादहर्ष [R1]. The आचार्य intends for the physician to understand that this specific affliction of the lower extremities arises directly from the combined aggravation of the कफ and वात doshas [R1].

By employing the dual descriptors हृष्यतः and प्रसुप्तवत्, the आचार्य covertly points to the physiological paradox created by combined Kapha and Vata, where Vata generates a subtle vibratory or tingling movement while heavy, dense Kapha induces blockage and profound numbness [R1, R4]. The choice of the term प्रसुप्तवत् with the pre-position प्र- suggests a deep, localized loss of functional awareness and tactile sensitivity in the extremities, mirroring a state of profound sleep superimposed upon active nerve channels [R1, R4]. Furthermore, by specifically designating this as कफवातप्रकोपजः, the author signals a departure from pure Vata disorders, instructing the astute physician that treatment must avoid purely dry, heating measures and instead incorporate judicious scraping and clearing modalities to resolve the dual obstruction [R1].

When aggravated वायु localizes in the shoulder region (अंसदेश), it dries up the shoulder ligaments and simultaneously contracts the blood vessels (सिरा) [R1]. Residing in that very location, this pathological process culminates in the manifestation of अवबाहुक, characterized by the impairment and immobility of the upper limb [R1].

In this chapter on the pathologies of Vata within the सुश्रुतसंहिता निदानस्थान, Acharya Sushruta explains the pathogenesis of deafness (बाधिर्य) [R1]. When either pure Vata or Vata associated with Kapha obstructs the auditory channel (शब्दवह स्रोतस्), it impairs auditory function and results in deafness [R1]. This verse thus attributes the specific condition of hearing loss to the obstruction of the sound-carrying channels by aggravated Vata, alone or combined with Kapha [R1].

Acharya Sushruta utilizes the phrase 'शब्दवहं स्रोतस्' to highlight that the pathophysiology of deafness stems from a functional occlusion of the specialized sensory channel rather than a mere structural defect in the ear itself. By employing 'शुद्धः श्लेष्मान्वितो वाऽपि', the Acharya underscores a dual etiological mechanism, indicating that Vata can either independently induce auditory failure through its intrinsic Ruksha and Khara qualities or act in synergy with dense, obstruction-prone Kapha. The use of 'आवृत्य तिष्ठति' further reveals that the chronicity and permanence of the hearing loss are directly tied to the stationary and encompassing nature of the doshic confinement within the pathway.

In the context of the Nidana Sthana of the सुश्रुतसंहिता, this verse defines the specific clinical feature of कर्णशूल (earache) arising from aggravated vayu [R1]. When the vitiated अनिल causes a piercing sensation across the lower jaw, temples, head, and neck while producing severe pain within both ears, the condition is precisely designated as कर्णशूलम् [R1]. This definition highlights how a localized manifestation of disturbed vayu creates intense, piercing pain radiating through the cranial and facial structures towards the ears [R1].

आचार्य सुश्रुत employs the participle ‘भिन्दन्निव’ along with the particle of comparison ‘इव’ to vividly indicate that the pain caused by aggravated वायु is not merely a dull ache, but possesses a sharp, splitting mechanical quality mimicking physical fracture across sensitive cranial tissues [R1]. In this verse from the Nidana Sthana chapter on the diagnosis of various diseases caused by the aggravated wind, Acharya Sushruta explains the pathological consequence when vayu becomes associated with kapha [R1]. When this kapha-associated vayu obstructs the sound-carrying channels (धमनीः शब्दवाहिनीः), it impairs a person's physical and vocal faculties, resulting in conditions such as physical inactivity, muteness, nasal speech, and stuttering (अक्रियकान्मूकमिन्मिणगद्गदान्) [R1].

By specifying that the *vayu* is accompanied by *kapha* (*सकफः*) and targets channels carrying sound (*शब्दवाहिनीः धमनीः*), the Acharya hints at a dual pathogenesis where heavy, cold *kapha* anchors the otherwise mobile *vayu*, transforming a dynamic functional disturbance into a dense structural stasis that suppresses both motor and vocal expression [R1]. The choice of the term *अक्रियकान्* alongside speech disorders suggests a profound neurological suppression akin to paralysis, wherein the vital channels governing both bodily movement and articulation are simultaneously choked by the sticky, phlegmatic obstruction [R1]. Furthermore, the graduation of speech impairment from complete silence (*मूकम्*) to nasal and broken articulation (*इन्मिणगद्गदान्*) reveals the Acharya's deep insight into how varying degrees of channel blockade dictate specific acoustic pathologies [R1].

Building upon the description of the downward-moving pain called तूनी, this verse explains that when the same pain originates in the anal and genital region but travels upward in the reverse direction with force toward the पक्वाशय, it is recognized as प्रतितूनी [R1, R2]. Thus, the आचार्य intends to clinically distinguish this upward-coursing variant of vata-induced colic pain.

A clinician should recognize this terrible and distinct condition, arising specifically from the obstruction of वायु, as आध्मान [R1].

The explicit designation of the condition as वातनिरोधजम्, rather than merely using a general term for vitiated Vata, highlights the mechanical nature of the pathology wherein a physical blockade of Vata's natural downward pathway creates a volatile and excessively painful emergency [R1]. 

By contrasting this deeply localized and dreadful condition with the movable and mixed pathologies described in adjacent verses, the आचार्य subtly instructs the clinician to differentiate pure mechanical obstruction of Vata from complex syndromes involving overlapping doshas [R1, R2].

तत् एव विमुक्तपार्श्वहृदयं आमाशयोत्थितं कफव्याकुलितानिलम् प्रत्याध्मानं विजानीयात् [R1]

तत् = that | एव = indeed | विमुक्तपार्श्वहृदयं = having freed sides and heart | आमाशयोत्थितम् = arisen from the stomach | कफव्याकुलितानिलम् = in which the wind is agitated by kapha | प्रत्याध्मानम् = Pratyadhmana | विजानीयात् = one should know [R1]

One should know that very [condition] arisen from the stomach, having freed sides and heart, in which the wind is agitated by kapha, as Pratyadhmana.

In the context of defining the specific varieties of udara roga and vatavyadhi within the Nidana Sthana of the Sushruta Samhita, the author characterizes the condition known as प्रत्याध्मानम् [R1]. Building upon the general presentation of आध्मानम् caused by the obstruction of vata [R3], आचार्य सुश्रुत distinguishes प्रत्याध्मानम् as originating in the stomach (आमाशय) where the aggravated wind is mingled and agitated by kapha [R1]. Unlike generalized distension, this specific manifestation is identified by the release or freedom of pressure in the sides (पार्श्व) and the heart region (हृदय) [R1].

उपसर्ग: वि (विमुक्तः) → specific release or freedom from affliction in those specific anatomical regions [R1]

उपसर्ग: उत् (उत्थितम्) → upward movement or origination [R1]
Contribution: Identifies the precise anatomical site of origin (stomach) for the pathology, distinguishing it from lower abdominal or intestinal origins [R1].

पद: कफव्याकुलितानिलम्
Synonyms: कफावृतानिलम्, कफसंसृष्टमारुतम्
Grammar: समस्तपदम् (कफेन व्याकुलितः अनिलाः यस्मिन् तत् - तृतीयाबहुव्रीहिः); नपुंसकलिङ्गम्, द्वितीया, एकवचनम्
धातु: व्यक्ल् / व्याकुल् (व्याकुलतायाम्) | धात्वर्थ: to be agitated, confused, disturbed; अनि (अन प्राणने) | धात्वर्थ: to breathe, move (wind/Vata) [R1]
उपसर्ग: वि + आ (व्याकुलित) → intense agitation or pervasiveness [R1]
Contribution: Explains the exact pathomechanism: Vata being agitated and obstructed by Kapha in the stomach [R1].

By employing the upasarga 'वि' in 'विमुक्तपार्श्वहृदयम्' and 'विजानीयात्', आचार्य सुश्रुत hints at a nuanced diagnostic differentiation where the absence of pain or pressure in the flanks and cardiac region serves as a crucial exclusionary sign to isolate the upper gastric involvement [R1]. The choice of the term 'प्रत्याध्मानम्' with the prefix 'प्रति-' subtly conveys a counter-movement or secondary reactive distension that mimics general abdominal bloating yet remains distinctly localized by the upward origination in the stomach ('आमाशयोत्थितम्') [R1]. Furthermore, the formulation 'कफव्याकुलितानिलम्' implies that the pathomechanism is not merely a passive obstruction by kapha, but an active, turbulent agitation of vata caused by the sticky, heavy nature of the conflicting dosha within the upper GI tract [R1].

9. मे — सुबन्तः — अस्मद्, षष्ठी/चतुर्थी एकवचनम्
मे देहे विचरतः तस्य आशुकारी मुहुश्चारी पक्वाधानगुदालयः लक्षणानि निबोध।

मे = from me (or of me / my) | देहे = in the body | विचरतः = moving | तस्य = of that (Vayu) | आशुकारी = acting swiftly | मुहुश्चारी = moving repeatedly | पक्वाधानगुदालयः = having the pakvadhana (large intestine) and the guda (anus) as his abode | लक्षणानि = the signs (symptoms) | निबोध = learn (understand).

Sentence meaning: Learn from me the signs of that Vayu moving in the body, which acts swiftly, moves repeatedly, and has the pakvadhana and guda as its abode.

Within the context of वातव्याधि निदान (Nidana of Vata disorders) in the सुश्रुतसंहिता, आचार्य सुश्रुत introduces the foundational characteristics of कोपित वायु (aggravated Vayu) moving throughout the body [R1, R4]. The author intends to highlight the fundamental attributes of वात — specifically its rapid action, recurrent mobility, and its primary residence in the पक्वाशय (large intestine) and गुद (anus) [R1, R3]. Understanding these inherent qualities is essential for the physician to recognise the general signs of वात प्रकोप before it manifests into specific diseases [R1].

By employing the compound terms आशुकारी and मुहुश्चारी, the Acharya implies that the pathology of वात is fundamentally characterized by unpredictable velocity and intermittent recurrence, mirroring its inherent nature of swiftness and instability [R1, R2]. The specific designation of पक्वाधान and गुद as its primary abode establishes that while वात moves systemically through the देह, its root disturbance originates from and returns to the lower alimentary tract, governing the expulsion and retention of bodily elements [R3]. Furthermore, the imperative formulation निबोध मे underscores the preceptor's intent that the physician must cultivate a sharp, focused clinical intuition to detect these subtle, dynamic manifestations before they fully consolidate into overt structural disease [R4].

In the context of defining the various manifestations of aggravated wind within the Nidana Sthana of the सुश्रुतसंहिता, the author characterizes the specific condition known as वाताष्ठीला [R1]. The Acharya intends for the physician to diagnose this disorder when a dense, knot-like, elevated, and elongated mass resembling a round stone forms and obstructs the external passages [R1]. This clinical sign helps differentiate the specific pathological behavior of obstructed vata within the abdominal and pelvic channels from neighboring conditions like प्रत्याध्मान [R1, R4].

Synonyms: उपरि, उच्चैः (upwards)
Grammar: अव्ययम् (दिशि)
धातु: ऋ (गतौ) | धात्वर्थः: to move
उपसर्ग: उत् (आधिक्ये, ऊर्ध्वम्) → denotes upward motion
Contribution: Specifies the direction of the growth or displacement of the mass within the abdomen.

पद: आयतम्
Synonyms: दीर्घम्, प्रसारितम् (extended, elongated)
Grammar: नपुंसकलिङ्गम्, द्वितीया विभक्तिः, एकवचनम् (सुबन्तः)
धातु: यम् (उपरमे / प्रापणे) | धात्वर्थः: to restrain or stretch
उपसर्ग: आङ् (समन्तात्) → indicates extensive spread
Contribution: Describes the elongated shape of the swelling along the anatomical tract.

पद: उन्नतम्
Synonyms: उच्चैःस्थितम्, उत्थितम् (elevated, raised)
Grammar: नपुंसकलिङ्गम्, द्वितीया विभक्तिः, एकवचनम् (सुबन्तः)
धातु: नम् (शब्दोपतापयोः / नम्रे) | धात्वर्थः: to bend or rise
उपसर्ग: उत् (उर्ध्वम्) → indicates upward elevation
Contribution: Highlights the protrusion or raised physical profile of the condition on the body's surface.

पद: वाताष्ठीलाम्
Synonyms: वातजनितामष्ठीलाम् (Vatasthila condition)
Grammar: स्त्रीलिङ्गम्, द्वितीया विभक्तिः, एकवचनम् (सुबन्तः); समस्तपदम् (कर्मधारयसमासः - वातप्रयुक्ता अष्ठीला इव)
विग्रहवाक्यम्: वातेन कृता अष्ठीला इव वाताष्ठीला
धातु: वा (गतिगन्धनयोः) / अश् (व्याप्तौ) | धात्वर्थः: to move / to pervade
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Names the specific clinical entity — a stone-like Vata-morbidity in the urinary/intestinal region.

पद: विजानीयात्
Synonyms: जानीयात्, अवगच्छेत् (one should recognize)
Grammar: विधिलिङ् (प्रशासने/प्रेरणे), प्रथमपुरुषः, एकवचनम् (तिङन्तः)
धातु: ज्ञा (ज्ञाने) | धात्वर्थः: to know, understand, or cognize
उपसर्ग: वि (विशेषे) → indicates precise, differentiated knowledge
Contribution: Directs the physician to accurately diagnose this specific condition through its defined physical signs.

पद: बहिः
Synonyms: बाह्ये, बहिर्देशे (outside, externally)
Grammar: अव्ययम् (स्थानार्थे)
धातु: बह (धारणे) | धात्वर्थः: to bear or carry outward (derived from Vedic/Classical usage)
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Establishes the spatial orientation of the obstruction relative to internal channels.

पद: मार्गान्
Synonyms: पन्थानः, स्रोतांसि (pathways, channels)
Grammar: पुंलिङ्गम्, द्वितीया विभक्तिः, बहुवचनम् (सुबन्तः)
धातु: मार्गू (मार्पणे) / मृग् (अन्वेषणे) | धात्वर्थः: to seek or traverse
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Refers to the bodily channels (srotas or passages) that are affected.

पद: अवरोधिनीम्
Synonyms: प्रतिरुधिनीम्, पिधायिनीम् (obstructing, blocking)
Grammar: स्त्रीलिङ्गम्, द्वितीया विभक्तिः, एकवचनम् (सुबन्तः); कृदन्तपदम् (णिच् + ण्वुल्र् प्रत्ययः)
धातु: रुध् (वरणे) | धात्वर्थः: to obstruct, check, or prevent movement
उपसर्ग: अव (अधोभावे / हीने / प्रतिबन्धे) → completely blocking or hemming in
Contribution: Captures the primary pathological action — the complete blockage of external channels by the morbid Vata mass.

By employing the prefix *वि-* with the root *ज्ञा*, the Acharya signals that recognizing *वाताष्ठीला* requires a precise, differential diagnosis that separates it from mere flatulence or generalized distention [R1, R3, R4]. The deployment of *घन* and *अष्ठीलावत्* together reveals that the aggravated Vata does not merely cause soft fluid accumulation, but imparts a stony, condensed hardness by seizing upon local structural elements [R1]. Furthermore, the specific combination of *ऊर्ध्वम्*, *आयतम्*, and *उन्नतम्* maps the precise spatial vector of the morbidity, showing how Vata forces the mass to elongate and thrust upward against anatomical pathways [R1, R7].

1st पाद- एनामेव रुजायुक्तां
2nd पाद- वातविण्मूत्ररोधिनीम्
3rd पाद- प्रत्यष्ठीलामिति वदे-
4th पाद- ज्जठरे तिर्यगुत्थिताम्

1. एनाम् — सुबन्तः — स्त्रीलिङ्गम् द्वितीया एकवचनम्
2. एव — अव्ययम् — अवधारणे (indeed)
3. रुजायुक्ताम् — सुबन्तः — स्त्रीलिङ्गम् द्वितीया एकवचनम्
4. वातविण्मूत्ररोधिनीम् — सुबन्तः — स्त्रीलिङ्गम् द्वितीया एकवचनम्
5. प्रत्यष्ठीलाम् — सुबन्तः — स्त्रीलिङ्गम् द्वितीया एकवचनम्
6. इति — अव्ययम् — प्रकारे (thus)
7. वदेत् — तिङन्तः — विधिलिङ्, प्रथमपुरुषः, एकवचनम्
8. जठरे — सुबन्तः — नपुंसकलिङ्गम् सप्तमी एकवचनम्
9. तिर्यगुत्थिताम् — सुबन्तः — स्त्रीलिङ्गम् द्वितीया एकवचनम्
(यः भिषक्) जठरे तिर्यगुत्थिताम् एनाम् एव रुजायुक्तां वातविण्मूत्ररोधिनीम् प्रत्यष्ठीलाम् इति वदेत्।

जठरे = in the abdomen | तिर्यगुत्थिताम् = arisen obliquely | एनाम् = this (condition) | एव = indeed | रुजायुक्ताम् = afflicted with pain | वातविण्मूत्ररोधिनीम् = obstructing flatus, feces, and urine | प्रत्यष्ठीलाम् = as Pratyashtheela | इति = thus | वदेत् = (one) should call |

One should call this condition, which is arisen obliquely in the abdomen, afflicted with pain, and obstructing flatus, feces, and urine, as Pratyashtheela.

In this verse from the Nidana Sthana of the सुश्रुतसंहिता, आचार्य सुश्रुत defines the specific abdominal condition known as प्रत्यष्ठीला [R1]. Continuing the context of urinary and flatulence-related obstructions, the author explains that when the pathological lump arises obliquely (तिर्यक्) within the abdominal cavity (जठर) rather than vertically, and is accompanied by severe pain along with the obstruction of flatus, feces, and urine, the physician should diagnose it as प्रत्यष्ठीला [R1]. Thus, it is distinguished by its oblique orientation and painful obstruction of the bodily excretions.

पद: एनाम्
Synonyms: इमाम्, असाम्
Grammar: स्त्रीलिङ्गम्, द्वितीया, एकवचनम् (सर्वनाम)
धातु: इ (गती) | धात्वर्थ: to go / to reach
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: This pronoun directly points to the specific clinical entity being described in the ongoing context [R1].

पद: एव
Synonyms: खलु, हि, निश्चयेन
Grammar: अव्ययम् (अवधारणे)
धातु: none | धात्वर्थ: none
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Emphasizes the exactness and certainty of the diagnosis [R1].

पद: रुजायुक्ताम्
Synonyms: वेदनान्विताम्, शूलसहिदाम्
Grammar: स्त्रीलिङ्गम्, द्वितीया, एकवचनम् (सुबन्तः)
समास: रुजया युक्ता (तृतीयातत्पुरुषसमासः); स्त्रीलिङ्गम् द्वितीया एकवचनम्; रुज् (रुजि रोगे) + अङ् + टाप् = रुजा, युज् (युर्जे योगे) + क्त = युक्ता
धातु: रुज् (रुजि रोगणे) / युज् (युर्जे योगे) | धात्वर्थ: to afflict with disease / to join
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Highlights that severe pain is an inseparable clinical feature distinguishing Pratyashtheela [R1].

पद: वातविण्मूत्ररोधिनीम्
Synonyms: वातमूत्रपुरीषप्रतिषेधिनीम्
Grammar: स्त्रीलिङ्गम्, द्वितीया, एकवचनम् (सुबन्तः)
समास: वातः च विट् च मूत्रं च = वातविण्मूत्रम् (इतरेतरद्वन्द्वः), वातविण्मूत्रं रुणद्धि इति वातविण्मूत्ररोधिनी (उपपदसमासः); स्त्रीलिङ्गम् द्वितीया एकवचनम्; रुध् (रुधिर् आवरणे) + णिच् + शतृ + ङीप् = रोधिनी
धातु: रुध् (रुधिर् आवरणे) | धात्वर्थ: to obstruct or block
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Specifies the triad of obstructions (flatus, stool, urine) caused by the swelling, marking the pathogenesis of Pratyashtheela [R1].

पद: प्रत्यष्ठीलाम्
Synonyms: प्रतिविशिष्टअष्ठीलाम्
Grammar: स्त्रीलिङ्गम्, द्वितीया, एकवचनम् (सुबन्तः)
समास: प्रतिगता अष्ठीलाम् (प्रादिसमासः / गतिसमासः) अथवा अष्ठीलायाः प्रति (अव्ययीभावः/कर्मधारयविशेषः); स्त्रीलिङ्गम् द्वितीया एकवचनम्
धातु: स्था (गतिनिवृत्तौ) | धात्वर्थ: to stand / to stay (as a firm mass)
उपसर्ग: प्रति (towards, in return, counter)
Contribution: The prefix 'प्रति' denotes a counter-mass or secondary firm projection relative to the classical Ashhtheela [R1, R2].

पद: इति
Synonyms: एवम्, प्रकारे
Grammar: अव्ययम् (प्रकारे)
धातु: none | धात्वर्थ: none
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Marks the conclusion of the naming and definition of the disease entity [R1].

पद: वदेत्
Synonyms: ब्रूयात्, कथयेत्
Grammar: तिङन्तः, विधिलिङ्, प्रथमपुरुषः, एकवचनम्
धातु: वद् (व्यक्तायां वाचि) | धात्वर्थ: to speak or to designate
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Directs the physician on the precise nomenclature to be adopted for this clinical presentation [R1].

पद: जठरे
Synonyms: कुक्षौ, उदरे
Grammar: नपुंसकलिङ्गम्, सप्तमी, एकवचनम् (सुबन्तः)
धातु: जठ् (दीप्तौ) | धात्वर्थ: to be fiery or to contain (abdomen)
उपसर्ग: none
Contribution: Locates the pathological manifestation precisely within the abdominal cavity [R1].

पद: तिर्यगुत्थिताम्
Synonyms: तिर्यग्गताम्, आत्यर्धिकतिर्यक्समुत्थिताम्
Grammar: स्त्रीलिङ्गम्, द्वितीया, एकवचनम् (सुबन्तः)
समास: तिर्यक् उत्थिता (प्रादिसमासः / गतिसमासः); स्त्रीलिङ्गम् द्वितीया एकवचनम्; तॄ (प्लवनतरणयोः) + क्विप् = तिर्यक्, उत् + स्था (गतिनिवृत्तौ) + क्त = उत्थिता
धातु: स्था (गतिनिवृत्तौ) | धात्वर्थ: to rise or emerge
उपसर्ग: उत् (upwards)
Contribution: Defines the oblique direction of the swelling's emergence in the abdomen, differentiating its pathway from upward or downward conditions [R1, R7].

आचार्य सुश्रुत employs the prepositional prefix 'प्रति' in 'प्रत्यष्ठीला' to subtly indicate a pathological variant that counters or deviates from the standard vertical orientation of वाताष्ठीला [R1, R2]. By specifying 'तिर्यगुत्थिताम्', the author intends to guide the clinician toward recognizing how an anatomical displacement along an oblique axis fundamentally alters the clinical severity, introducing acute pain (रुजायुक्ताम्) and total stagnation of excretions [R1]. This deliberate choice underscores a diagnostic principle where spatial vector changes within the abdominal cavity dictate distinct disease manifestations requiring precise clinical differentiation [R1].
